definition_zh: 生意；商业；公司、企业；事务；职责
definition_en: the activity of buying and selling goods and services, a company that does this, matters that need attention, or the thing that is properly someone's concern
core_image: 街角小店开门营业，柜台上放着账本与零钱
scene: 街角的小店从早开到晚，生意一直不错。 The little shop on the corner does good business all year.
sceneCN: 这里 business 是「生意；商业」（第 1 个义项：买卖商品与服务的活动）；句意为街角那家小店一年到头生意都不错。

pos.zh: 名词：生意；商业；公司；事务；职责

derivatives.zh: 由 business 与 man 组合而成，义为「商人」
由 business 与 like 组合而成，义为「讲求效率的；公事公办的」
与 business 同源，义为「忙碌的」，business 原就是由它派生

senses.title: Buying and selling
senses.definition: the activity of buying and selling goods or services
senses.definitionCN: 买卖商品或服务的活动
senses.example: The little shop does good business all year.
senses.exampleCN: 那家小店一年到头生意都不错。
senses.why: Business first meant the state of being busy, then the work a person is busy with, and finally trade.
senses.whyCN: business 最初指「忙碌的状态」，接着指一个人忙于做的事，最后指买卖。

senses.title: A company
senses.definition: a company that makes, buys or sells goods or services
senses.definitionCN: 制造、购买或出售商品与服务的公司
senses.example: He runs a small business with his brother.
senses.exampleCN: 他和弟弟一起经营一家小企业。
senses.why: When the buying and selling is set up as an organization, the activity itself becomes the name of the firm.
senses.whyCN: 当买卖被组织成一家机构时，这项活动本身就成了这家公司的名称。

senses.title: Matters to deal with
senses.definition: things that need to be dealt with or discussed
senses.definitionCN: 需要处理或讨论的事情
senses.example: Let us finish the business of the meeting first.
senses.exampleCN: 我们先把会议的事务办完。
senses.why: The old sense of being busy with something survived: any matter that keeps you occupied is your business.
senses.whyCN: 「忙于某事」的旧义保留了下来：任何让你有事可做的事情都叫 business。

senses.title: What properly concerns you
senses.definition: the thing that is properly your concern and not another person's
senses.definitionCN: 本该由你负责、而不是别人的事
senses.example: How I spend my money is my own business.
senses.exampleCN: 我怎么花钱是我自己的事。
senses.why: What a person is busy with is his own concern, so the word also marks the line between my affairs and yours.
senses.whyCN: 一个人忙于的事就是他自己的关切，所以这个词也划出了我的事与你的事之间的界线。

intro.en: Business was formed from busy, and it has moved from the state of being busy to the world of trade.
intro.cn: business 由 busy 构成，词义从「忙碌的状态」一路走到「买卖」。

items.en: Bisignes meant the state of being busy, and also care and anxiety.
items.cn: bisignes 意为忙碌的状态，也指操心与忧虑。

items.en: The noun was built from bisig, busy, with the ending -nes.
items.cn: 这个名词由 bisig（忙碌的）加上词尾 -nes 构成。

items.en: From being busy the word moved to the work one is busy with.
items.cn: 词义从「忙碌」转向一个人忙于其中的工作。

items.en: In the seventeenth century business came to mean trade and commercial dealing.
items.cn: 十七世纪时 business 开始指贸易与商业往来。

items.en: Today business covers trade, firms, matters to handle and personal concerns.
items.cn: 今天 business 覆盖贸易、公司、待办事务与个人分内之事。

note.en: The first group collects words close in shape or sound; the second group collects words about trade.
note.cn: 第一组收拼写或读音接近的词，第二组收与商业有关的词。

entries.definition: Having a lot to do, the word business came from.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「忙碌的」，business 正由它派生。

entries.definition: Efficient and practical in the way work is done.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「讲求效率的」，由 business 加 like 构成。

entries.definition: The state of having much to do.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「忙碌」，读音与 business 接近但意思不同。

entries.definition: The buying and selling of goods between people or countries.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「贸易」。

entries.definition: Trade on a large scale, used in a formal tone.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「商业」，多用于正式语境。

entries.definition: An organization that sells goods or services.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「公司」。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the recorded history, the real family and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用有记录的历史、真实词族和这个词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: Business is busy plus ness: first the state of being busy, then the work itself.
normal.cn: business 就是 busy 加 ness：先指忙碌的状态，再指那件工作。

normal.en: Old English bisignes also meant care and worry, which busy work often brings.
normal.cn: 古英语 bisignes 也指操心与忧虑，而忙碌的工作常常带来这些。

normal.en: By the seventeenth century the busy work had become trade.
normal.cn: 到十七世纪，忙于其中的工作就变成了买卖。

normal.en: It often pairs with do, trip, small and own.
normal.cn: 它常与 do、trip、small、own 搭配。

normal.en: Spell b-u-s-i-n-e-s-s; the i is not pronounced, so it sounds like bizness.
normal.cn: 拼写是 b-u-s-i-n-e-s-s，其中 i 不发音，读起来像 bizness。

abstract.en: See a small shop open its shutters at dawn with a ledger on the counter: that shop is doing business.
abstract.cn: 想象一家小店清晨拉起卷帘门，柜台上放着账本：这家店就在做生意。

abstract.en: Change the ledger into a private letter and the same word becomes my own business.
abstract.cn: 把账本换成一封私人信件，同一个词就变成了「我自己的事」。

abstract.en: Say the word aloud, then let the open shutters bring the meaning back.
abstract.cn: 先把这个词读出声，再让那扇拉起的卷帘门把意思带回来。

examples.en: The little shop does good business all year.
examples.cn: 那家小店一年到头生意都不错。

examples.en: He runs a small business with his brother.
examples.cn: 他和弟弟一起经营一家小企业。

examples.en: How I spend my money is my own business.
examples.cn: 我怎么花钱是我自己的事。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「必死呢死」——一天到晚忙个不停的事：生意

root: business 由古英语 bisig（忙碌的）加词尾 -nes 构成，原作 bisignes，意为「忙碌的状态」，也指操心与忧虑。词义后来从「忙碌」转向「一个人忙于其中的工作」，十七世纪又发展为「贸易与商业往来」。今天它既指生意与公司，也指需要处理的事务，以及本该由某人负责的分内之事。

sensesIntro.en: All four senses of business grow from one picture: someone busy at a counter with work that is his own.
sensesIntro.cn: business 的四个义项都从同一个画面生长出来：一个人守在柜台后，忙着一件属于他自己的事。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small shop busy at its counter from morning to night
core.cn: 核心意象：一家小店从早到晚在柜台后忙碌

branches.en: THE TRADE: buying and selling is the modern centre of the word.
branches.cn: 贸易线：买卖是这个词现代的核心义。

branches.en: THE FIRM: organized trade becomes a company.
branches.cn: 公司线：被组织起来的买卖成为企业。

branches.en: THE MATTER: whatever keeps you busy is a piece of business.
branches.cn: 事务线：任何让你忙碌的事都是一件 business。

branches.en: THE LINE: what is properly yours marks a boundary.
branches.cn: 界线线：该由你负责的事划出一条边界。

branches.en: THE SHOP: activity and organization sit behind one counter.
branches.cn: 店铺线：活动与机构都立在同一个柜台之后。

intro.en: Business is a derived noun, so the items below are its endings and the words it joins.
intro.cn: business 是派生名词，下面列出的是它的词尾以及与之组合的词。

latinIntro.en: Latin negotium means business and otium means leisure; they are parallels, not the source of business.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 negotium 意为「事务、生意」，otium 意为「闲暇」，它们是平行词，不是 business 的来源。

items.example: It is the base of business.

definition_zh: 成员；会员；成员国；肢体；议员；集合元素；构件；家庭成员
definition_en: one of the parts or people that make up a group or a body
core_image: 一张长桌四周坐满人，每把椅子背后贴着写了名字的纸牌
scene: 点名时秘书念出一个名字，长桌尽头有人举手，墙上的名册随即在那一行后面打了一个勾。 As the secretary read the roll, a hand went up at the far end of the table, and the list on the wall received a tick beside that member.
sceneCN: 这里 member 指「团体中的一名成员」（第 1 个义项）；句意为点名时长桌尽头有人举手应到，墙上的名册在该成员那一行打勾。可辨识物件：长桌、名册、铅笔、举起的手；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 成员；会员；成员国；肢体；议员；集合元素；构件；家庭成员
成员的；作定语的（如成员国）

derivatives.zh: 会员身份（member + -ship，由「人」转为「身份」）
肢解；切去肢体（dis- + member，由「肢体」义派生）

senses.title: One among many
senses.definition: a person who belongs to a group, team or organization
senses.definitionCN: 属于某团体、队伍或组织的一个人
senses.example: Every member of the team signed the card.
senses.exampleCN: 队里的每一名成员都签了卡片。
senses.why: The Latin word for a limb was applied to people as parts of a community, and this is the sense that dominates today.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语指「肢体」的词被用来指共同体中的个人，这成了今天最主要的义项。

senses.title: A state among states
senses.definition: a country or organization that belongs to a larger union
senses.definitionCN: 属于更大联盟的国家或组织
senses.example: The member states met to revise the treaty.
senses.exampleCN: 各成员国开会修订这项条约。
senses.why: Once a body can be a part of a larger body, whole states take the name that once belonged to persons.
senses.whyCN: 既然一个机构可以是更大机构的一部分，整个国家也就用上了原属个人的称呼。

senses.title: A limb of the body
senses.definition: an arm, leg or other part of the body
senses.definitionCN: 手臂、腿或身体的其他部位
senses.example: The old anatomy text speaks of the body and its members.
senses.exampleCN: 那本古老的解剖学著作谈到身体及其四肢。
senses.why: This is the oldest layer: the Latin noun named a limb before it named a person in a group.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的一层：这个拉丁名词先指肢体，后指团体中的人。

senses.title: A seat in the house
senses.definition: a person elected or appointed to a legislative assembly
senses.definitionCN: 经选举或任命进入立法机构的个人
senses.example: The member for the northern district spoke last.
senses.exampleCN: 北部选区的议员最后发言。
senses.why: Legislatures borrow the plain word for a group member and make it a title with a constituency attached.
senses.whyCN: 立法机构借用这个表示团体成员的普通词，并给它加上选区，使之成为头衔。

senses.title: An element of a set
senses.definition: an object that belongs to a mathematical set
senses.definitionCN: 属于某一数学集合的对象
senses.example: Each member of the set shares one property.
senses.exampleCN: 集合中的每个元素都共有一种性质。
senses.why: Mathematics needed a neutral word for what is inside a set, and the everyday noun was precise enough.
senses.whyCN: 数学需要一个中性词来指集合内部的东西，而这个日常名词已经足够精确。

senses.title: A part of a frame
senses.definition: one of the beams or parts that make up a structure
senses.definitionCN: 构成某一结构的梁或其他部件
senses.example: Every member of the truss carries part of the load.
senses.exampleCN: 桁架的每个构件都承担一部分荷载。
senses.why: Engineering returns to the limb sense: a frame is a body, and its beams are its members.
senses.whyCN: 工程学回到了「肢体」义：框架是一个躯体，梁就是它的肢体。

senses.title: One of the household
senses.definition: a person belonging to a family or household
senses.definitionCN: 属于某个家庭或住户的人
senses.example: The household has four members, two of them children.
senses.exampleCN: 这个家庭有四名成员，其中两名是孩子。
senses.why: The smallest group a person belongs to is a household, and the word scales down without changing.
senses.whyCN: 一个人所属的最小团体就是家庭，这个词缩小尺度而含义不变。

senses.title: One of a species group
senses.definition: an organism belonging to a particular group in taxonomy
senses.definitionCN: 在分类学上属于某一类群的生物
senses.example: This species is a member of the rose family.
senses.exampleCN: 这个物种是蔷薇科的一员。
senses.why: Natural history treats a family as a body and its species as members, completing the same metaphor.
senses.whyCN: 博物学把一个科当作躯体、把其中的物种当作成员，完成了同一个比喻。

intro.en: Member comes from Latin membrum 'limb, part of the body', which Latin also used for a person as a part of a community. English borrowed it through Old French. Its deeper origin is not settled. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: member 来自拉丁 membrum「肢体、身体的一部分」，拉丁语也用这个词指作为共同体之部分的个人。英语经古法语借入。其更深来源尚无定论。下列年代均为约数。

items.en: Membrum is well recorded for a limb. The extension to a person who is a part of a group is also Latin, not a later English invention.
items.cn: membrum 指肢体有充分书证。把它扩展到「团体之部分的个人」也发生在拉丁语中，并非英语后来的创造。

items.en: The deeper origin of membrum is generally thought to involve a root for cutting or dividing, but the form is a reconstruction and different handbooks word it differently.
items.cn: membrum 的更深来源一般被认为与表示「切割、划分」的词根有关，但该形式属重构，各家手册的表述也不一致。

items.en: Old French membre carried both the limb sense and the social sense, and English took the word in the thirteenth century.
items.cn: 古法语 membre 同时带有「肢体」义与社会义，英语在十三世纪借入这个词。

items.en: From the sixteenth century the word spread to legislatures, mathematics and engineering, each borrowing the part-of-a-whole image.
items.cn: 从十六世纪起，这个词扩展到立法机构、数学与工程学，每一处都借用了「整体之一部分」的意象。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper root): the pre-Latin form is a reconstruction, so the family image at the base is inferred rather than demonstrated.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词根）：前拉丁语的形式属重构，因此词底的家庭意象属推断而非实证。

note.en: Group one holds the same-root forms and one look-alike built on an unrelated root; group two holds words for people who belong to something.
note.cn: 第一组是同根形式，另加一个建在无关词根上的形近词；第二组是表示「属于某处的人」的词。

entries.definition: The status of being a member; member is the person, membership is what that person holds.
entries.definitionCN: 成员的身份；member 是人，membership 是此人所拥有的身份。

entries.definition: To cut a body into parts, built directly on the limb sense of the Latin noun.
entries.definitionCN: 把身体切成数块，直接建在这个拉丁名词的「肢体」义上。

entries.definition: From re- plus memor 'mindful', not from membrum: it means to recall, and only the sound connects it.
entries.definitionCN: 由 re- 加 memor「留心的」构成，并非来自 membrum：意为回想，只有读音把它联系起来。

entries.definition: Also from memor 'mindful'; the shared letters suggest a limb root that is not there.
entries.definitionCN: 同样来自 memor「留心的」；相同的字母让人以为有「肢体」词根，其实并没有。

entries.definition: An organization attached to a larger one; a member can be a person or a body, while an affiliate is always an organization.
entries.definitionCN: 附属于更大机构的组织；member 可以是人也可以是机构，而 affiliate 总是机构。

entries.definition: A colleague or linked firm without formal membership; a member holds a defined place on a roll.
entries.definitionCN: 无正式成员身份的同事或关联公司；member 在名册上拥有明确的位置。

entries.definition: A companion or peer, often in a learned society; fellow stresses equality, member stresses inclusion.
entries.definitionCN: 同伴或同侪，常用于学会；fellow 强调平等，member 强调被纳入。

entries.definition: A person who takes part in an event; a participant need not be on any roll, while a member is.
entries.definitionCN: 参与某项活动的人；参与者不必在名册上，而成员则在名册上。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin limb word, the real institutional compounds, and the real derived forms.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁「肢体」词、真实的机构复合词，以及真实的派生形式。

normal.en: A member is a limb of the body of the group: the metaphor is the same at both scales.
normal.cn: 成员是团体的「肢体」：这个比喻在两个尺度上完全一致。

normal.en: The oldest sense is anatomical, which is why dismember means cutting off limbs, not expelling people.
normal.cn: 最古老的义项是解剖学上的，因此 dismember 指切去肢体，而不是开除成员。

normal.en: Compound phrases: member state, family member, staff member, founding member.
normal.cn: 复合搭配：成员国、家庭成员、工作人员、创始成员。

normal.en: A member of parliament is a member first and a representative second, which is why the title keeps the plain word.
normal.cn: 议会议员先是「成员」，其次才是代表，因此这个头衔保留了那个朴素的词。

normal.en: The plural is regular, and the possessive adds an apostrophe with the possessive ending.
normal.cn: 复数按常规变化，所有格则在词尾加撇号与属格标记。

abstract.en: Picture a long table where every chair has a name card taped to its back.
abstract.cn: 想象一张长桌，每把椅子背后都贴着一张写有名字的卡片。

abstract.en: Picture a truss bridge seen as a skeleton, each beam a limb holding the whole up.
abstract.cn: 想象一座桁架桥被看成一具骨架，每根梁都是撑起整体的一肢。

abstract.en: Picture a family photograph in which each face occupies one place in the frame.
abstract.cn: 想象一张全家福，每张脸都在画面里占一个位置。

examples.en: She became a member of the research group in her second year.
examples.cn: 她在第二年成为研究小组的成员。

examples.en: The member states disagreed over the wording of the clause.
examples.cn: 各成员国对条款的措辞意见不一。

examples.en: The fall injured a member of his left hand.
examples.cn: 那次跌倒伤到了他左手的一处肢体。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「member = mem（记忆）+ ber」——被记住、被写进名册的人 → 成员、会员

root: 拉丁 membrum「肢体、身体的一部分」；由「躯体之一肢」引申为「团体之一员」。更深词根属重构，不作定论。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one limb: a person on the roll, a state inside a union, the anatomical limb itself, a seat in a legislature, an element in a set, a beam in a frame, a face in a household, and a species inside a family.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕「一肢」展开：名册上的人、联盟中的国家、解剖意义上的肢体、立法机构中的一席、集合中的元素、框架中的一根梁、家庭中的一张面孔，以及一个科之内的一个物种。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a long table where every chair carries a name card on its back.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张长桌，每把椅子背后都贴着写有名字的卡片。

branches.en: PERSONS AND HOUSEHOLDS: the person on the roll, and the smallest group that person belongs to.
branches.cn: 个人与家庭：名册上的人，以及此人所归属的最小团体。

branches.en: STATES AND UNIONS: a whole country holding a place inside a larger body.
branches.cn: 国家与联盟：整个国家在更大机构中占据一席。

branches.en: THE OLDEST LAYER: the limb itself, the literal body part behind the metaphor.
branches.cn: 最古老的一层：肢体本身，也就是比喻背后那个字面的身体部位。

branches.en: THE SEAT IN THE HOUSE: a legislator whose title keeps the plain word for a group member.
branches.cn: 议会中的一席：立法者的头衔保留了「团体成员」这个朴素说法。

branches.en: PARTS OF STRUCTURED WHOLE: a set element, a structural beam, and a species inside a family.
branches.cn: 结构整体的各个部分：集合元素、结构构件，以及一个科之内的物种。

intro.en: Member is the Latin limb word reshaped in English, and its family runs from anatomy to institutions.
intro.cn: member 是拉丁语「肢体」一词在英语中的变形，其词族从解剖学一直延伸到制度。

latinIntro.en: Latin membrum yields member and dismember; -ship and non- build the social forms. The Latin noun is third-declension in -um, not a verb.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 membrum 衍生出 member 与 dismember；-ship 与 non- 构成社会义的形式。这个拉丁名词属 -um 第二变格法，并非动词。

items.example: The Latin noun is the base of the family.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁名词是词族的基础。

items.example: Every member of the team signed the card.
items.exampleCN: 队里的每一名成员都签了卡片。

items.example: The members voted on the proposal.

definition_zh: 检查；审查；考查；检验；盘问
definition_en: to look at something closely and in detail in order to judge its condition, quality or truth
core_image: 一架老式天平，指针停在刻度之间，旁边放着待称的信封与放大镜
scene: 一位技师把送来的旧钟拆开，逐枚查看齿轮的磨损痕迹。 A conservator examines each gear under a magnifier before ordering repairs.
sceneCN: 技师拆开旧钟，逐枚查看齿轮磨损；句中的 examine 指「仔细查看以判断状况」（第 1 个义项：近距离细看以了解状态）。图中可辨识物件：拆开的机芯、放大镜、镊子、记录纸。

pos.zh: 检查；审查；考查；检验；盘问

senses.title: Look closely at a thing
senses.titleCN: 近距离细看以判断状况
senses.definition: to inspect something closely in order to learn its condition
senses.definitionCN: 近距离查看某物，以了解其状况
senses.example: A conservator examines each gear under a magnifier.
senses.exampleCN: 修复师在放大镜下逐枚检查齿轮。
senses.why: the Latin verb came from the noun for the tongue of a balance, so the earliest picture is a needle settling to show how much something weighs.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁动词来自表示「天平指针」的名词，因此最早的意象是一根指针停稳，显示某物有多重。

senses.title: Test a student's knowledge
senses.definition: to question a student in order to measure what has been learned
senses.definitionCN: 通过提问来测量学生学到了什么
senses.example: The committee examines candidates in both written and oral rounds.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会用笔试与口试两轮考查候选人。
senses.why: a balance decides value by an exact measure, and an examiner does the same with a candidate's knowledge, which is why the school sense came early.
senses.whyCN: 天平用精确的衡量判定价值，主考人对考生的知识做的也是同一件事，因此学校义很早就出现了。

senses.title: Investigate formally
senses.definition: to go through evidence in an official inquiry
senses.definitionCN: 在正式调查中逐项查验证据
senses.example: Lawyers examined the invoices line by line.
senses.exampleCN: 律师逐行审查了这些发票。
senses.why: the weighing image fits legal inquiry: each item is placed on the scale and its weight argued.
senses.whyCN: 称量的意象正合法律调查：每一件证据都被放上天平，再争论它的分量。

senses.title: Check a patient
senses.definition: to inspect a person's body to find signs of illness
senses.definitionCN: 查看人体以发现疾病的迹象
senses.example: The doctor examined the ankle and sent him for a scan.
senses.exampleCN: 医生检查了脚踝，又让他去做扫描。
senses.why: the medical sense is the general inspection sense narrowed to the body, where signs must be found before a judgement is made.
senses.whyCN: 医学义是把一般查看收窄到身体：必须先找到迹象，才能作出判断。

senses.title: Analyse data critically
senses.definition: to study information closely to find patterns or errors
senses.definitionCN: 细究信息以找出规律或错误
senses.example: The team examined the readings for seasonal drift.
senses.exampleCN: 团队细查读数，寻找季节性漂移。
senses.why: data has to be weighed in the same way as goods: the verb keeps its old sense of testing rather than merely seeing.
senses.whyCN: 数据也要像货物一样被称量：这个动词保留的是「检验」而非「看见」的旧义。

senses.title: Question a witness
senses.definition: to question a witness formally, especially in court
senses.definitionCN: 正式询问证人，尤指在法庭上
senses.example: The defence examined the witness for two hours.
senses.exampleCN: 辩方盘问证人达两小时。
senses.why: courtroom question and balance share an origin: both force an account to show its weight under pressure.
senses.whyCN: 法庭讯问与天平同源：二者都迫使一份陈述在压力下显出分量。

senses.title: Inspect goods
senses.definition: to check goods for quality or damage before accepting them
senses.definitionCN: 在接受货物前查看其质量或损坏情况
senses.example: The buyer examined the crates before signing.
senses.exampleCN: 买方在签字前检验了木箱。
senses.why: trade kept the most literal sense, because a merchant must look at what is being weighed and paid for.
senses.whyCN: 商贸保留了最字面的意义，因为商人必须看清被称量、被付钱的东西。

senses.title: Weigh a proposal
senses.definition: to consider an idea carefully before deciding
senses.definitionCN: 在作决定前仔细考虑一个想法
senses.example: The board examined every option before voting.
senses.exampleCN: 董事会在投票前审议了每一个选项。
senses.why: the balance image turns abstract: options are placed one after another on the same scale until a choice settles.
senses.whyCN: 天平的意象在此抽象化：选项被逐一放上同一架秤，直到选择落定。

intro.en: Examine comes from Latin examinare 'to weigh, test', built on examen, the noun for the tongue or needle of a balance, which itself goes back to exigere 'to drive out, to weigh'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: examine 来自拉丁 examinare「称量、检验」，其名词 examen 指天平的指针或舌杆，而 examen 又可追溯至 exigere「驱出、称量」。年代为约数。

items.en: Exigere combined ex- 'out' with agere 'to drive, do' and meant 'to drive out, to demand, to weigh exactly'. The weighing sense grew from the demand for exact measure.
items.cn: exigere 由 ex-「出」与 agere「驱使、做」构成，意为「驱出、索求、精确称量」。称量义由对精确衡量的要求发展而来。

items.en: Examen named the tongue of a balance, the pointer that settles when the two pans hold equal weight.
items.cn: examen 指天平的舌杆，即两盘等重时停稳的那根指针。

items.en: From the noun came examinare 'to weigh, to test, to inquire into', used for both goods and arguments.
items.cn: 由这个名词产生 examinare「称量、检验、查究」，既用于货物也用于论辩。

items.en: Old French examiner carried the verb into English in the fourteenth century, first in the legal and scholarly senses.
items.cn: 古法语 examiner 在十四世纪把这个动词带入英语，最初用于法律与学术场合。

items.en: By the sixteenth century the verb covered questioning a candidate and inspecting a patient, both extensions of testing.
items.cn: 到十六世纪，这个动词已涵盖考查考生与检查病人，二者都是「检验」的延伸。

items.en: The detail that examen meant specifically the balance tongue is generally accepted, but the deeper origin of agere and the exact route from exigere to examen are not fully settled; forms offered for a pre-Latin root are reconstructions.
items.cn: examen 特指天平舌杆这一细节一般认为是可靠的，但 agere 的更早来源以及从 exigere 到 examen 的确切路径尚无定论；为其拉丁语之前词根给出的形式属重构形式。

note.en: Group one holds the derived family and two words that merely look similar but come from a different verb; group two holds verbs of looking and testing that differ in pressure and purpose.
note.cn: 第一组是派生词族，以及两个只是形似、其实出自另一动词的词；第二组是查看与检验类动词，压力与目的各不相同。

entries.definition: The act or result of examining, and also the paper sat in a school; it cannot stand where the verb is needed.
entries.definitionCN: 检查或审查的行为与结果，也指学校里的试卷；不能代替动词。

entries.definition: The one who questions or inspects, not the act itself.
entries.definitionCN: 指提问或检查的人，而非行为本身。

entries.definition: Looks close but comes from eximere 'to take out', not from examen; an example is something taken out for display.
entries.definitionCN: 形近但出自 eximere「取出」，与 examen 无关；example 是被取出展示的样本。

entries.definition: Also from eximere: to take someone out of an obligation, with no notion of weighing.
entries.definitionCN: 同样出自 eximere：把某人从义务中取出，不含称量之意。

entries.definition: A formal look, often by an authority checking standards; examine is broader and can include testing.
entries.definitionCN: 正式查看，常指权威方查标准；examine 范围更广，可含检验。

entries.definition: To look into a matter over time, following leads; it stresses process more than the single act of weighing.
entries.definitionCN: 指沿线索在一段时间里查办某事，更强调过程而非单次称量。

entries.definition: To examine with suspicion and great closeness, adding doubt that examine does not carry.
entries.definitionCN: 带着怀疑极仔细地查看，多出 examine 所无的疑虑。

entries.definition: To make something show its quality by use or trial; examine may only look and judge.
entries.definitionCN: 通过使用或试用让某物显出品质；examine 可能只是查看并判断。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations here are the real balance image, the real Latin steps, the real family and the real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想取自真实的天平意象、真实的拉丁演变、真实词族与真实固定搭配。

normal.en: examen was the tongue of a balance: to examine is to put something on the scale.
normal.cn: examen 是天平的舌杆：examine 就是把某物放上秤。

normal.en: ex- 'out' plus agere 'drive': to drive a matter out into the open where it can be weighed.
normal.cn: ex-「出」加 agere「驱使」：把一件事驱到明处，好称它的分量。

normal.en: The family runs examination, examiner, examinee, exam, cross-examine.
normal.cn: 词族包括 examination、examiner、examinee、exam、cross-examine。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the settings: examine evidence, examine a patient, examine a witness.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出场景：审查证据、检查病人、询问证人。

normal.en: The passive is common in reports: the findings were examined by two reviewers.
normal.cn: 报告中常用被动式：研究结果由两位审稿人审查。

abstract.en: Picture a needle that will not settle until every doubt has been placed on one pan or the other.
abstract.cn: 想象一根指针，直到所有疑问都被放上这盘或那盘才肯停稳。

abstract.en: Picture a jeweller's loupe left on a tray of loose stones, each one already weighed.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚珠宝放大镜搁在一盘散石上，每颗都已称过。

abstract.en: Picture a courtroom where a sentence is literally hung on the scales.
abstract.cn: 想象一间法庭，判决就悬在天平上。

examples.en: The panel examined the proposal for hidden costs.
examples.cn: 小组审议了提案，寻找隐藏成本。

examples.en: She examined the transcript against the recording.
examples.cn: 她对照录音检查了文字稿。

examples.en: The vet examined the horse before the sale.
examples.cn: 兽医在售前检查了这匹马。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「ex（出）+ amine（像「阿门」）」——把东西拿出来放到天平上称一称 → 检查、审查、考查

root: 拉丁 exigere「驱出、称量」→ 名词 examen「天平指针」→ 动词 examinare「称量、检验」→ 古法语 examiner → 英语 examine；agere 的更深来源与 exigere 到 examen 的确切路径尚无定论，相关词根形式属重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses hang on one instrument: something is placed on a balance, and the same gesture is then used on a clock, a student, a file of evidence, an ankle, a data set, a witness, a crate and finally on a list of options.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项挂在同一件器具上：把某物放上天平，同一个动作随后用于旧钟、学生、证据卷宗、脚踝、数据集、证人、木箱，最后用于一列选项。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a balance needle that only settles after everything has been put on the pans.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根天平指针，非等一切都被放上秤盘不肯停稳。

branches.en: PHYSICAL CHECK: a gear and a crate are both looked over before a judgement is passed.
branches.cn: 实物查验：齿轮与木箱都要先被看过，才有判断。

branches.en: QUESTIONING: a candidate and a witness are pressed to show what they carry.
branches.cn: 盘问：考生与证人都被追问，要他们显出分量。

branches.en: PAPER AND NUMBERS: invoices and readings must be gone through line by line.
branches.cn: 纸面与数字：发票与读数都得逐行过一遍。

branches.en: BODY: the same inspection narrows to signs of illness in a patient.
branches.cn: 身体：同样的查看收窄为病人身上的疾病迹象。

branches.en: CHOICE: options are weighed one after another until the needle settles.
branches.cn: 抉择：选项被逐一称量，直到指针停稳。

intro.en: The verb is a Latin prefix and root plus two suffixes, and the same pieces build the whole examining family.
intro.cn: 这个动词由拉丁前缀、词根再加两个后缀构成，同一批部件也造出整个「检查」词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin exigere and examen supply the core; the English suffixes -ation, -er and -ee build the nouns.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 exigere 与 examen 提供核心；英语中的名词后缀与表人后缀造出各个名词。

items.example: The prefix drives the action outward.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把动作向外驱出。

items.example: Agere is the root of the weighing image.
The verb entered English through French.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词经法语进入英语。

items.meaning: the act of testing or inspecting
items.exampleCN: 这场审查持续了三小时。

items.example: The examiner read the answers twice.
items.exampleCN: 主考人把答案读了两遍。

items.example: Each examinee received a numbered seat.
items.exampleCN: 每位应试者都拿到一个编号座位。

items.example: The exam was moved to Friday.

items.meaning: to question a witness for the other side
items.meaningCN: 对另一方证人进行交叉询问
items.exampleCN: 律师交叉询问了那名职员。

latinEntries.meaning: the tongue of a balance; a weighing

definition_zh: 负责的；有责任的；可靠的
definition_en: having a duty, being the cause, or being reliable
core_image: 一个人手里握着一串钥匙，要对每扇门负责
scene: 值夜班的护士负责检查每一间病房。 The nurse on night duty is responsible for checking every ward.
sceneCN: 这里 responsible 是「负责的」（第 1 个义项：负有职责、须对某事负责）；句意：值夜班的护士负责检查每一间病房。

pos.zh: 负责的；有责任的；可靠的

senses.title: Having a duty or being in charge
senses.definition: having the job of looking after something or someone
senses.definitionCN: 负有照看某物或某人的职责
senses.example: She is responsible for the whole team.
senses.exampleCN: 她负责整个团队。
senses.why: The word comes from a Latin verb meaning to answer in return, so the responsible person is the one who must answer.
senses.whyCN: 这个词来自意为「回以答复」的拉丁动词，因此负责的人就是必须作出交代的人。

senses.title: Being the cause of something
senses.definition: being the cause of an event, especially a bad one
senses.definitionCN: 是某事件的原因，尤指坏事件
senses.example: Heavy rain was responsible for the flood.
senses.exampleCN: 大雨是这场洪水的原因。
senses.why: The one who must answer for an event is often the one who caused it.
senses.whyCN: 必须为事件作出交代的人，往往就是造成事件的人。

senses.title: Reliable and sensible
senses.definition: able to be trusted to act sensibly and carefully
senses.definitionCN: 可以被信任，能明智谨慎地行事
senses.example: We need a responsible driver for the night trip.
senses.exampleCN: 夜间出行我们需要一位可靠的司机。
senses.why: A person who answers for their actions is likely to act carefully.
senses.whyCN: 能为自己的行为负责的人，往往会谨慎行事。

senses.title: Accountable to someone
senses.definition: required to report to a person or authority
senses.definitionCN: 须向某人或某机构汇报的
senses.example: The committee is responsible to the whole school.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会对全校负责。
senses.why: Answering in return also means answering to a higher authority.
senses.whyCN: 回以答复也意味着向更高权威作出交代。

intro.en: Responsible comes from Latin respondere, to answer in return, through French responsable, so it means answerable.
intro.cn: responsible 经法语 responsable 来自拉丁语 respondere（回以答复），因此意为「须作出交代的」。

items.en: Respondere means to answer in return.
items.cn: respondere 意为回以答复。

items.en: Responsum means an answer.
items.cn: responsum 意为回答。

items.en: Responsable means answerable.
items.cn: responsable 意为应负责的。

items.en: Responsible covers duty and cause.
items.cn: 英语 responsible 涵盖职责与原因。

items.en: Modern English adds the sense of being reliable.
items.cn: 现代英语增加了「可靠」的含义。

note.en: Responsible is an answerable adjective, close to its noun family and to words for accountability.
note.cn: responsible 是表示「应负责」的形容词，与自身名词词族以及表示问责的词相邻。

entries.definition: a duty
entries.definitionCN: 责任

entries.definition: in a responsible way
entries.definitionCN: 负责地

entries.definition: not responsible
entries.definitionCN: 不负责任的

entries.definition: required to explain one's actions
entries.definitionCN: 应作解释的；负有责任的

entries.definition: able to be trusted
entries.definitionCN: 可靠的

entries.definition: legally responsible
entries.definitionCN: 负有法律责任的

normalIntro.en: Responsible means answerable: if something goes wrong, you are the one who must respond.
normalIntro.cn: responsible 意为「须作出交代」：如果出了问题，你就是必须回应的人。

normal.en: Responsible for means in charge of or the cause of.
normal.cn: responsible for 表示负责或造成。

normal.en: Responsible to means answerable to a person.
normal.cn: responsible to 表示向某人负责。

normal.en: A responsible person acts carefully.
normal.cn: responsible person 行事谨慎。

normal.en: The noun responsibility is the duty itself.
normal.cn: 名词 responsibility 指责任本身。

normal.en: Compare accountable: accountable stresses reporting, responsible is broader.
normal.cn: 对比 accountable：accountable 强调汇报，responsible 范围更广。

abstract.en: Picture a person holding keys to every door in a building.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人拿着整栋楼每扇门的钥匙。

abstract.en: Imagine a driver checking the mirror before moving.
abstract.cn: 想象司机起步前检查后视镜。

abstract.en: Think of a captain standing steady at the wheel.
abstract.cn: 想象船长稳稳站在舵轮旁。

examples.en: The teacher is responsible for thirty students.
examples.cn: 这位老师负责三十名学生。

examples.en: Poor planning was responsible for the failure.
examples.cn: 计划不周是失败的原因。

examples.en: She is a responsible and careful worker.
examples.cn: 她是一位可靠而细心的员工。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「response + ible」——出了事必须「回应」的人，就是负责的；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 re-（回）＋ spondere（承诺）→ respondere（回以答复）→ 法语 responsable → 英语 responsible，核心义「须作出交代的」。

sensesIntro.en: Responsible first means having a duty, then being the cause, then being reliable, and finally being answerable to someone.
sensesIntro.cn: responsible 先指负有职责，再指是原因，再指可靠，最后指向某人负责。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person holding keys and answering for every door.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人拿着钥匙，为每扇门负责。

branches.en: Being in charge is the main sense.
branches.cn: 负责掌管是主要义项。

branches.en: Being the cause is the explanatory sense.
branches.cn: 是原因是解释性义项。

branches.en: Being reliable is the character sense.
branches.cn: 可靠是品格义项。

branches.en: Being answerable to an authority is the reporting sense.
branches.cn: 向权威负责是汇报义项。

branches.en: A person in charge should also be dependable.
branches.cn: 负责的人也应该可靠。

intro.en: Responsible is a Latin answering adjective reshaped by French, with a large English family.
intro.cn: responsible 是经法语改造的拉丁语「答复」形容词，拥有庞大的英语词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin respondere means to answer in return, from spondere, to promise.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 respondere 意为回以答复，源于 spondere（承诺）。

items.exampleCN: responsible 保留应负责的含义。

definition_zh: 折叠；合拢；交叠（双臂）；折痕；羊栏
definition_en: to bend paper, cloth or hands so one part lies on another; also, a line made by folding, or a pen for sheep
core_image: 把纸或布对折，让两层叠在一起
scene: 写完信，她把信纸对折再对折，才装进窄窄的信封。 Please fold the letter in half before you seal it.
sceneCN: 这里 fold 是动词「折叠」（第 1 个义项：弯折使一部分压在另一部分上）；句意为封口前请把信对折。

derivatives.zh: 由 fold 加名词后缀构成，义为「文件夹」
由 fold 加动名词后缀构成，义为「可折叠的」
由 un- 加 fold 构成，义为「展开；显露」
由 two 加 fold 构成，义为「两倍的；双重的」

senses.title: To bend one part over another
senses.definition: to bend something flexible so that one part covers another
senses.definitionCN: 把柔软之物弯折，使一部分盖住另一部分
senses.example: He folded the map along the crease.
senses.exampleCN: 他沿折痕把地图折起来。
senses.why: The core image is one flat layer lying down onto another.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是一层平面倒伏叠上另一层。

senses.title: To bring arms or hands together
senses.definition: to bring the arms, hands or wings closely together
senses.definitionCN: 把双臂、双手或翅膀合到一起
senses.example: She folded her hands on the desk.
senses.exampleCN: 她双手交叠放在桌上。
senses.why: Flat limbs lay one over another exactly like folded paper.
senses.whyCN: 扁平的手臂相互叠放，与折纸的动作如出一辙。

senses.title: A line where something is folded
senses.definition: a line or crease made by folding
senses.definitionCN: 折叠后留下的线条
senses.example: Iron out the folds in the shirt.
senses.exampleCN: 把衬衫上的褶熨平。
senses.why: The act leaves its mark, and the mark got the verb's name.
senses.whyCN: 动作留下痕迹，痕迹便以动词命名。

senses.title: A pen for sheep
senses.definition: an enclosure for sheep on a farm
senses.definitionCN: 农场里圈羊的围栏
senses.example: The sheep returned to the fold at dusk.
senses.exampleCN: 黄昏时羊群回到羊栏。
senses.why: A fence closes in on itself like a folded wall around the flock.
senses.whyCN: 围栏像一道折拢的墙，把羊群圈在其中。

senses.title: To close a business
senses.definition: to close because of failure, as a company does
senses.definitionCN: 公司因经营失败而关门
senses.example: The bakery folded after two years.
senses.exampleCN: 那家面包店两年后倒闭了。
senses.why: A business folding up closes like folded paper, pressed flat and finished.
senses.whyCN: 企业收摊如同纸被折平压扁，就此了结。

intro.en: Fold comes from an old English verb about doubling things over.
intro.cn: fold 来自古英语中表示把东西叠起的动词。

items.en: Old English had faldan or fealdan, to fold or double over.
items.cn: 古英语作 faldan 或 fealdan，意为折叠、对折。

items.en: It traces to common Germanic falthan, shared with German falten and Dutch vouwen.
items.cn: 它可追溯到共同日耳曼语 falthan，与德语 falten、荷兰语 vouwen 同源。

items.en: Old English also had falod for the sheep pen, a related but separate word.
items.cn: 古英语另有 falod 指羊栏，是相关但独立的词。

items.en: Middle English merged the spellings into fold for both senses.
items.cn: 中古英语把两个含义的拼写合并为 fold。

items.en: Modern English added the business sense of folding up, like paper pressed shut.
items.cn: 现代英语增加了企业收摊的比喻义，如纸被折平。

note.en: Fold sits near several sound-alike words.
note.cn: fold 与几个音近词相邻。

abstract.en: See sheep streaming back through a narrow gate.

examples.cn: 把纸对折，再折成四分之一。

examples.en: He folded his arms and listened.
examples.cn: 他交叉双臂听着。

examples.en: The little shop folded last month.

definition_zh: 保卫；看守；防护；警惕；卫兵；防护装置
definition_en: to keep someone or something safe from danger or attack; a person or thing that protects
core_image: 一名卫兵笔直站在大门前，双手如盾挡在危险与门之间
scene: 博物馆展厅入口站着一位站姿笔挺的工作人员，提醒大家不要触碰展柜。 The guard stopped the visitors from touching the glass case.
sceneCN: 这里 guard 是「警卫、看守者」（第 3 个义项：负责保护的人）；句意是警卫阻止游客触碰玻璃展柜。

pos.zh: 卫兵；警卫；防护装置；警惕

senses.title: To protect from danger
senses.definition: to keep a person or place safe from harm
senses.definitionCN: 使人或地方免受伤害
senses.example: Dogs guard the farm at night.
senses.exampleCN: 狗在夜里看守农场。
senses.why: The image is a shield standing between danger and what is protected, so the verb means blocking harm.
senses.whyCN: 画面是挡在危险与保护对象之间的盾，动词义就是拦截伤害。

senses.title: To watch carefully
senses.definition: to watch a person or place to stop escape or theft
senses.definitionCN: 看住人或地方以防逃跑或偷窃
senses.example: Two officers guard the prison gate.
senses.exampleCN: 两名警官看守监狱大门。
senses.why: A shield must also have eyes; standing watch is the watching half of protecting.
senses.whyCN: 盾还要有眼睛，站岗放哨就是「保护」里看的部分。

senses.title: A person who protects
senses.definition: a person whose job is to protect a place or person
senses.definitionCN: 以保护某地或某人为职责的人
senses.example: The bank guard opened the door for us.
senses.exampleCN: 银行保安为我们开了门。
senses.why: The doer of the action becomes the name of the person, as often happens in English.
senses.whyCN: 执行动作的人顺理成章变成名词，英语里常见这种转变。

senses.title: A device that protects
senses.definition: a piece of equipment that covers a dangerous part of a machine
senses.definitionCN: 盖住机器危险部位的装置
senses.example: Always use the blade guard on the saw.
senses.exampleCN: 用锯子时务必装上锯片护罩。
senses.why: If a person can guard, a barrier can too; the shield image turns into hardware.
senses.whyCN: 人能守卫，屏障也能，盾的画面变成了实物装置。

senses.title: Careful attention to prevent mistakes
senses.definition: care taken to avoid a mistake or danger
senses.definitionCN: 为避免错误或危险而保持的小心
senses.example: Keep guard against careless spelling in exams.
senses.exampleCN: 考试要防范粗心的拼写错误。
senses.why: Protection begins in the mind; staying alert is protecting before danger arrives.
senses.whyCN: 保护始于内心，警惕就是在危险到来之前先行设防。

intro.en: Guard came into English through French from a Germanic root about watching over.
intro.cn: guard 经法语进入英语，源自日耳曼语词根，意为「看护」。

items.en: A West Germanic root wardon meant to watch over and protect.
items.cn: 西日耳曼语词根 wardon 意为看护、保护。

items.en: Old French garder meant to keep, watch, and protect, borrowing the Germanic root.
items.cn: 古法语 garder 意为保存、看守、保护，借用了日耳曼词根。

items.en: Old Norse vartha, from the same Germanic stock, gave English the close relative ward.
items.cn: 同一日耳曼语系的古诺斯语 vartha 给英语带来近亲 ward。

items.en: Middle English took guard from Old French in the fourteenth century for soldiers watching a place.
items.cn: 十四世纪中古英语从古法语借入 guard，指看守之地的士兵。

items.en: Modern English kept both the person and the device senses and added guard against for caution.
items.cn: 现代英语保留「人」与「装置」两义，并增加 guard against 表防范。

definition_zh: 允许；许可；正式批准；书面批文；权限
definition_en: the act of allowing someone to do something, or the official right to do it that an authority grants
core_image: 一把钥匙被放进掌心：门还锁着，但你已经有权把它推开
scene: 美术馆的展厅里，讲解员把三脚架拦在门外，指着墙上一行小字提醒参观者。 Photographs are allowed only with written permission from the museum.
sceneCN: 这里是「正式许可、批准」（第 2 个义项：机构给出的正式准许）；句意为只有拿到博物馆的书面许可才能拍照。画面的重点是门口被拦下的三脚架和墙上那行小字。

pos.zh: 允许；许可；批准；书面批文；权限

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁词干 permiss- 加 -ive 构成，义为「宽容的；放任的」
由同一词干加 -ible 构成，义为「可允许的；容许的」
与 permission 同出拉丁语 permittere，作动词指「允许」，作名词指「许可证」；两者同源但不是同一词的词形变化
由 permissive 加 -ness 构成，义为「宽容；放任」

senses.title: The act of allowing someone to do something
senses.definition: the act of agreeing that someone may do something, without necessarily putting it in writing
senses.definitionCN: 同意某人可以做某事的行为，不一定落实为文字
senses.example: She gave me permission to use her desk while she was away.
senses.exampleCN: 她不在的时候允许我用她的桌子。
senses.why: Latin permittere joins per-, through, with mittere, to send or let go; the idea is letting something pass out of your control.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 permittere 由表示「穿过」的 per- 与表示「送出、放开」的 mittere 合成，本义是让某件事从自己的掌控中放行，所以这个词天生带着点头放人的动作感。

senses.title: Official authorization from an authority
senses.definition: the official right to do something that a person or body in authority gives you
senses.definitionCN: 由有权的个人或机构给予的做某事的正式权利
senses.example: No one may film inside the court without permission from the judge.
senses.exampleCN: 未经法官批准，任何人不得在法庭内拍摄。
senses.why: Once the letting-through happens inside an institution, the same noun names the authorization the body issues rather than a private nod.
senses.whyCN: 当「放行」发生在机构内部，这个名词就从私人的点头变成了机构发出的授权，因此在规章语境里它几乎等同于批准。

senses.title: A written or formal grant, often countable
senses.definition: a formal document or stated allowance that records the right to do something
senses.definitionCN: 记录做某事权利的正式文件或明确许可
senses.example: The crew needed three separate permissions to shut the street for a night.
senses.exampleCN: 摄制组需要三份不同的批文才能封街一夜。
senses.why: Permission can be counted when the thing counted is not the consent itself but the separate grants, one for each activity.
senses.whyCN: 当被计数的不是「同意」本身，而是逐项开出的批文时，permission 就可以数了，一次活动一份，于是出现复数形式。

senses.title: Access rights inside a computer system
senses.definition: the rights that control what a user may read, change or delete on a computer system
senses.definitionCN: 控制用户在计算机系统中可以读取、修改或删除哪些内容的权利
senses.example: The folder refuses to open until an administrator changes its permissions.
senses.exampleCN: 在管理员更改文件夹权限之前，它打不开。
senses.why: Computing borrowed the institutional sense literally: the system checks whether your account has been let through to a file.
senses.whyCN: 计算机几乎是照搬机构义的逻辑：系统检查你的账号是否被放行到某个文件，于是同一个词变成了权限设置。

intro.en: Permission descends from Latin permissio, the action noun of permittere; it shares that verb with the English verb permit but is not the verb plus a suffix.
intro.cn: permission 源自拉丁语 permissio，那是动词 permittere 的动作名词；它与英语动词 permit 共享同一个拉丁动词，并不是由 permit 直接加后缀变来的。

items.en: Mittere meant to send or to let go, and it lies under a large Latin family of release and sending.
items.cn: mittere 意为送出、放开，许多表示释放与送出的拉丁词都由它衍生。

items.en: Adding per-, through, produced permittere, to let something pass through, and therefore to allow it.
items.cn: 加上表示「穿过」的 per-，构成 permittere：让某物通过，因而引申为允许。

items.en: The action noun permissio named the letting-through itself and is the direct source of the English noun.
items.cn: 动作名词 permissio 指放行这件事本身，是英语名词的直接来源。

items.en: Old French carried the noun as permission and handed it to Middle English in the fourteenth century.
items.cn: 古法语以 permission 的形式承接这个名词，并在十四世纪交给中古英语。

items.en: English kept the noun for consent, later allowed countable grants, and in the twentieth century added computer access rights.
items.cn: 英语保留名词表示同意的用法，后来发展出可数的批文义，二十世纪又添上计算机访问权一义。

note.en: The first group collects words built on the same Latin verb of letting through; the second collects words about consent, approval and access.
note.cn: 第一组收同一个拉丁动词派生出的词；第二组收表示同意、批准与准入的词。

entries.definition: The verb, and separately the noun for a licence, both built on Latin permittere.
entries.definitionCN: 直接建于拉丁语 permittere 之上的动词，以及另一个表示许可证的名词。

entries.definition: Allowing a lot of freedom and not punishing behaviour strictly.
entries.definitionCN: 给予很大自由、不严格约束行为的；宽容的。

entries.definition: Allowed by a rule or by law.
entries.definitionCN: 规则或法律所允许的。

entries.definition: A task someone is sent to carry out, from the Latin verb of sending.
entries.definitionCN: 派某人去完成的任务，出自同一个表示送出的拉丁动词。

entries.definition: Agreement to something happening, given by someone free to refuse.
entries.definitionCN: 对某事发生的同意，由有权拒绝的人给出。

entries.definition: Official power or approval to act, usually written down.
entries.definitionCN: 行动的正式权力或批准，通常见诸文字。

entries.definition: Official permission to go ahead, especially after a check.
entries.definitionCN: 尤指经审查后获得的继续进行的正式许可。

entries.definition: A document that allows an activity, usually paid for.
entries.definitionCN: 允许某项活动的证件，通常需要付费取得。

normalIntro.en: The word is held together by a Latin verb of letting through, and its relatives keep returning to gates, grants and keys.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词靠一个表示放行的拉丁动词支撑，同族词反复回到门禁、批文与钥匙上。

normal.en: Per- means through in Latin, so permission is literally a letting-through: the gate opens and you walk in.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 per- 意为穿过，所以 permission 字面上就是放行：门开了，你走进去。

normal.en: The noun keeps the miss- stem of mittere, to send; the same stem hides in mission and in the verb permit.
normal.cn: 这个名词保留了 mittere（送出）的 miss- 词干，同一词干也藏在 mission 与动词 permit 里。

normal.en: You ask for permission and you receive permission, and those two verbs box in most of its everyday use.
normal.cn: 请求许可、获得许可，这一对动词几乎框住了它在日常里的全部用法。

normal.en: Without permission and with permission are fixed pairs, and the noun after with takes no article.
normal.cn: 未经许可与经许可都是固定搭配，with 后面直接跟不带冠词的名词。

normal.en: Spoken English often prefers to say that someone is allowed to do something, while written rules prefer the noun.
normal.cn: 口语常说某人被允许做某事，而书面规章更偏爱这个名词。

abstract.en: Permission is a door held open by someone else: the room was always there, but you could not enter until that hand moved.
abstract.cn: permission 是别人替你扶住的门：房间一直在那里，可那只手不动，你就进不去。

abstract.en: The word measures the distance between wanting to do something and being entitled to do it.
abstract.cn: 这个词量出的，是想做某件事与有权做某件事之间的距离。

abstract.en: Inside a computer the same idea becomes a switch: access is either granted or refused, with nothing in between.
abstract.cn: 在计算机里，同一个念头变成一个开关：访问权要么被授予，要么被拒绝，中间没有余地。

examples.en: Nobody leaves the base without written permission.
examples.cn: 没有书面许可，谁也不能离开基地。

examples.en: The council finally gave permission for the market to reopen.
examples.cn: 市政会终于批准市场重新开放。

examples.en: She was refused permission to sit the exam early.
examples.cn: 她提前参加考试的申请被拒绝了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「怕米审」——想从米仓取米，得先过一道审查，怕米审不过就一粒也拿不走；permission 就是许可。

root: 拉丁语 permittere（per- 穿过 + mittere 送出）意为放行、允许，其名词形 permissio 经古法语 permission 进入英语；同族词多与送出、放行有关。

sensesIntro.en: From a private nod to an official grant and then to a line of code, the word keeps one idea: something is let through.
sensesIntro.cn: 从私人的点头到机构的批准，再到一行代码，这个词始终守着一个意思：某样东西被放行了。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a key placed in your palm while the door stays shut until you turn it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一把钥匙被放进掌心，门还锁着，等你转动手腕。

branches.en: a friend nodding so you may borrow the chair
branches.cn: 朋友点头，你才把那把椅子搬走

branches.en: a signature at the bottom of an official form
branches.cn: 公文末尾的一个签名

branches.en: the same yes, spoken once and printed once
branches.cn: 同一个「可以」，一次说出口，一次印成纸

branches.en: a locked folder waiting for an administrator
branches.cn: 一个锁着的文件夹等着管理员

branches.en: a gate, whether of wood or of software
branches.cn: 一道门，木头做的或软件做的都一样

intro.en: A Latin prefix of passage, a Latin verb of sending and a noun ending that turns the act into a thing hold the word together.
intro.cn: 表示穿过的拉丁前缀、表示送出的拉丁动词，以及把动作变成名词的词尾，共同撑起这个词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family is well recorded: mittere, permittere and permissio all survive inside English borrowings.
latinIntro.cn: 这一族的拉丁词有清楚记录：mittere、permittere、permissio 都通过借词留在了英语里。

definition_zh: 快乐的；令人愉快的；乐意的
definition_en: happy and smiling; making people feel happy; said in a happy way
core_image: 脸上挂着阳光般的笑，走进房间就把气氛点亮
scene: 值日生擦完黑板，笑眯眯地回到座位，连老师都被感染了。 She gave a cheerful smile when she finished cleaning the board.
sceneCN: 这里 cheerful 是「快乐的」（第 1 个义项：面带笑容、心情好）；句意为她擦完黑板后露出快乐的微笑。

pos.zh: 快乐的；令人愉快的；乐意的

derivatives.zh: 由 cheerful 加 -ly 构成，义为「快乐地；爽快地」
由 cheerful 加 -ness 构成，义为「快乐；开朗」

senses.title: Happy and smiling
senses.definition: feeling or showing happiness, with a smile
senses.definitionCN: 感到或显出快乐，面带笑容
senses.example: She gave a cheerful smile when she finished cleaning the board.
senses.exampleCN: 她擦完黑板后露出快乐的微笑。
senses.why: The word piles the happy mood onto the face that shows it, matching its old meaning of expression.
senses.whyCN: 这个词把快乐的情绪叠加在显露它的脸上，正与其古义「神情」相合。

senses.title: Making people feel happy
senses.definition: making a place or time feel bright and happy
senses.definitionCN: 让地方或时光显得明亮快乐
senses.example: The yellow curtains make the room cheerful.
senses.exampleCN: 黄色的窗帘让房间显得明快。
senses.why: A thing that fills a room with the happy feeling borrows the mood word for itself.
senses.whyCN: 让房间充满快乐情绪之物，便借用了这种情绪词来描述自身。

senses.title: Said or done in a willing, bright way
senses.definition: willing and happy to do something, without complaining
senses.definitionCN: 乐意且愉快地做某事，毫无怨言
senses.example: He gave a cheerful yes to the extra job.
senses.exampleCN: 他爽快地答应接下额外的活儿。
senses.why: A person with a bright mood agrees easily, so the mood word extends to willing action.
senses.whyCN: 心情明亮的人答应得爽快，情绪词便延伸到乐于做事的态度上。

intro.en: Cheerful adds the 'full of' suffix to cheer, which once meant the face and its mood.
intro.cn: cheerful 在 cheer（古义为面容与心情）之上加了「充满」后缀。

items.en: Greek kara meant the head, the ancestor of the face idea.
items.cn: 希腊语 kara 意为头，是「面容」意象的源头。

items.en: Old French chere meant the face and the expression on it.
items.cn: 古法语 chere 指面容及其神情。

items.en: Middle English chere meant mood or spirits, as in of good chere.
items.cn: 中古英语 chere 指心情或情绪，如 of good chere。

items.en: The suffix -ful, meaning full of, was added to make cheerful.
items.cn: 中古英语后期加上意为「充满」的后缀 -ful，构成 cheerful。

items.en: Modern English uses cheerful for people, places and willing actions.
items.cn: 现代英语用 cheerful 形容人、环境与乐意之举。

note.en: The first group collects words close in shape or sound; the second group collects happy words.
note.cn: 第一组收拼写或读音接近的词，第二组收快乐类词。

entries.definition: The root word meaning shout of joy.
entries.definitionCN: 名词/动词，义为「欢呼」，是 cheerful 的词根。

entries.definition: A small round red fruit.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「樱桃」，拼写与 cheerful 词首相近。

entries.definition: Paying attention to avoid mistakes.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「小心的」，与 cheerful 词尾结构相同。

entries.definition: Feeling pleasure or contentment.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「快乐的」，与 cheerful 相近。

entries.definition: Cheerful and lively, often at festivals.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「欢乐的」，多用于节日气氛。

entries.definition: Dark and sad.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「阴郁的」，cheerful 的反义词。

normalIntro.en: Remember cheerful by its root and family.
normalIntro.cn: 借助词根与词族记忆 cheerful。

normal.en: cheerful is cheer plus -ful, full of cheer.
normal.cn: cheerful 是 cheer 加 -ful，即充满欢乐。

normal.en: cheerfully describes doing things happily.
normal.cn: cheerfully 形容愉快地做事。

normal.en: a cheerful room is a bright, happy place.
normal.cn: cheerful room 指明亮宜人的房间。

normal.en: careful and cheerful share the same -ful ending.
normal.cn: careful 与 cheerful 共用后缀 -ful。

normal.en: she stayed cheerful even on rainy days.
normal.cn: even on rainy days, she stayed cheerful：即使在雨天她也保持乐观。

abstract.en: Picture sunlight spilling through a clean window onto a desk.
abstract.cn: 想象阳光透过明净的窗户洒到课桌上。

abstract.en: Hear a whistled tune between classes.
abstract.cn: 仿佛听见课间有人吹起的口哨曲。

abstract.en: Feel the lightness of a nod that says yes gladly.
abstract.cn: 感受爽快点头应允时的轻盈。

examples.en: She gave a cheerful smile when she finished cleaning the board.
examples.cn: 她擦完黑板后露出快乐的微笑。

examples.en: The yellow curtains make the room cheerful.
examples.cn: 黄色的窗帘让房间显得明快。

examples.en: He always speaks in a cheerful voice.
examples.cn: 他说话总是带着愉快的语气。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「齐儿福」——齐声欢笑都是福气，真是快乐的 cheerful。

root: 希腊语 kara（头）→ 拉丁语 cara（面容）→ 古法语 chere → 中古英语 chere + -ful → 现代英语 cheerful；同族词有 cheer（欢呼）、cheerfully（快乐地）。

sensesIntro.en: Cheerful spreads from a smiling face to bright places and willing answers.
sensesIntro.cn: cheerful 由带笑的脸延伸到明快的环境与爽快的应允。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a face full of joy
core.cn: 核心意象：写满喜悦的一张脸

branches.en: A happy person
branches.cn: 快乐的人

branches.cn: 明快宜人的环境

branches.cn: 爽快的应允

branches.cn: 带着微笑完成值日

branches.en: Bright colours and music
branches.cn: 明快的颜色与音乐

intro.cn: cheerful 展示了意为「充满」的后缀 -ful 加在欢乐词根 cheer 上。

latinIntro.en: It has no Latin root of its own; the suffix -ful is Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: 它自身无拉丁词根；后缀 -ful 是日耳曼语的。

definition_zh: 年龄；时代；年老；长时间
definition_en: how old someone or something is, or a period of history, or being old
core_image: 生日蛋糕上插着蜡烛
scene: 生日那天，蛋糕上插着十二根蜡烛。 She is twelve years of age.
sceneCN: 这里 age 是「年龄」（第 1 个义项：活了多少年）；句意为她十二岁。

pos.zh: 名词：年龄；时代；年老；长时间

senses.title: How old someone is
senses.definition: the number of years a person or a thing has lived
senses.definitionCN: 人或事物已经存在的年数
senses.example: She is twelve years of age.
senses.exampleCN: 她十二岁。
senses.why: Age comes from Latin aetas, the length of a life, so it first means the number of years one has lived.
senses.whyCN: age 来自拉丁语 aetas「生命的长短」，先指一个人活了多少年，就是年龄。

senses.title: A period of history
senses.definition: a long period of history with a shared character
senses.definitionCN: 具有共同特征的一段长历史时期
senses.example: The age of steam changed the world.
senses.exampleCN: 蒸汽时代改变了世界。
senses.why: The same length is put on a whole society, which gives the sense of a historical age.
senses.whyCN: 把这种长度放到整个社会上，就成了历史的时代。

senses.title: To grow old
senses.definition: to become older
senses.definitionCN: 变得年长
senses.example: Worry can age a person.
senses.exampleCN: 忧虑会让人变老。
senses.why: The noun became a verb for the process of gaining years.
senses.whyCN: 名词转为动词，指年岁增长的过程，就是变老。

senses.title: A very long time
senses.definition: used in ages for a long time in speech
senses.definitionCN: 口语中用于 ages，表示很长时间
senses.example: We have not met for ages.
senses.exampleCN: 我们很久没见了。
senses.why: In speech, many years are stretched into the plural ages for a very long time.
senses.whyCN: 口语把许多年拉长成复数 ages，就是很久。

intro.en: The recorded history of age is set out below; the deeper origin is marked where it is uncertain.
intro.cn: 下面是 age 有记录的历史；更早的来源存疑处已作标注。

items.en: Aetas meant a lifetime or a period of time.
items.cn: aetas 意为一生的时间或一段时期。

items.en: Old French used aage for a person's years.
items.cn: 古法语用 aage 指一个人的年岁。

items.en: English borrowed age for the length of a life.
items.cn: 英语十三世纪借入 age，指生命的长度。

items.en: The word widened to mean a period of history.
items.cn: 这个词扩大为指历史上的一个时期。

items.en: Today it also covers old age and a long wait.
items.cn: 今天它也指老年与漫长的等待。

note.en: The first group collects forms that look or sound alike; the second group collects words with a nearby meaning.
note.cn: 第一组收形近或音近的词，第二组收意义相近的词。

entries.definition: A very long time, in common speech.
entries.definitionCN: 口语中指很长的时间。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning old.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，意为年老的。

entries.definition: The process of growing old.
entries.definitionCN: 指变老的过程。

entries.definition: A long period with a shared character.
entries.definitionCN: 指具有共同特征的长时期。

entries.definition: A length of time with a start and an end.
entries.definitionCN: 指有起点与终点的一段时间。

entries.definition: The plain word for the time someone has lived.
entries.definitionCN: 指某人已活过的年数的朴素说法。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the recorded form, the real family and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用有记录的词形、真实的词族和这个词实际出现的搭配。

normal.cn: aetas 意为一生的时间或一个时期，所以 age 指生命或时代的长短。

normal.en: The same family also gives aged and aging.
normal.cn: 同一词族还给出 aged 与 aging。

normal.en: It often appears in the phrase at the age of.
normal.cn: 它常出现在「在……岁时」这个搭配里。

normal.en: Spell it as it sounds: keep every letter of age in order.
normal.cn: 按读音拼写：把 age 的每个字母按顺序保留。

normal.en: Use it when you mean: how old someone or something is, or a period of history, or being old.
normal.cn: 当你想表达「年龄」时用它。

abstract.cn: 同一幅画面在一句里可以是字面意思，在另一句里可以是比喻。

abstract.en: Say the word aloud first, then let the picture bring the meaning back.

definition_zh: 正确地；无误地
definition_en: in a right way, without mistakes
core_image: 指南针稳稳指向北，分毫不差
scene: 实验课上同学们轮流读出量筒的刻度。 You must read the scale correctly in a science test.
sceneCN: 这里 correctly 是「正确地」（第 1 个义项：以无误的方式）；句意是科学考试中必须准确读数。

derivatives.zh: 去掉 -ly 的原形，义为「正确的」
加否定前缀 in- 构成，义为「错误地」

senses.title: In a right way without mistakes
senses.definition: in the way that is right, without errors
senses.definitionCN: 以正确的方式，没有错误
senses.example: She answered every maths question correctly.
senses.exampleCN: 她正确地答出了每道数学题。
senses.why: The adverb keeps the made-straight image: the action runs straight, with no crooked steps.
senses.whyCN: 副词保留扶正的意象：动作笔直进行，没有歪斜环节。

senses.title: In the standard or accepted way
senses.definition: according to the accepted rule or standard
senses.definitionCN: 按照公认的规则或标准
senses.example: Please hold the tennis racket correctly.
senses.exampleCN: 请按规范握好网球拍。
senses.why: What is straight by the rule is also what everyone accepts as proper.
senses.whyCN: 规则上笔直的也是大家认可得体的。

senses.title: Working as it should
senses.definition: working in the way it is designed to work
senses.definitionCN: 按设计的方式运行
senses.example: The new projector works correctly in every classroom.
senses.exampleCN: 新投影仪在每个教室都运行正常。
senses.why: A machine made straight runs straight, so correctly also describes devices.
senses.whyCN: 造得周正的机器运转顺畅，correctly 也形容设备。

intro.cn: correctly 只是给 correct 加上副词后缀。

items.cn: 词基 correct 来自 corrigere，扶正。

items.cn: correct 于十四世纪进入英语。

definition_zh: 地址；演说；称呼；处理
definition_en: the place where someone lives, or a speech, or to deal with a problem
core_image: 信封上写着一行清楚的地址
scene: 信封上写着一行清楚的地址。 The address on the envelope was easy to read.
sceneCN: 这里 address 是「地址」（第 1 个义项：住址或所在地）；句意为信封上的地址很容易看清。

pos.zh: 动词：处理；对……讲话；写地址

senses.title: The place where someone lives
senses.definition: the details of where a person or a place is
senses.definitionCN: 关于某人或某处所在位置的详细信息
senses.example: Write your address on the form.
senses.exampleCN: 把你的地址写在表格上。
senses.why: Ad- means toward and the old French verb meant to direct, so pointing words toward a place gives the sense of an address.
senses.whyCN: ad- 表示「向」，古法语动词意为「指向」，把住处指向一个地方，就是地址。

senses.title: A formal speech
senses.definition: a speech made to a group on an occasion
senses.definitionCN: 在某个场合对一群人发表的讲话
senses.example: The head gave an address to the school.
senses.exampleCN: 校长对全校发表了讲话。
senses.why: Pointing a speech toward a whole group gives the formal sense of an address.
senses.whyCN: 把一段话指向整个群体，就是正式的演说。

senses.title: A way of speaking to someone
senses.definition: the words used when speaking or writing to a person
senses.definitionCN: 对某人说话或写信时使用的称谓
senses.example: The letter began with a polite address.
senses.exampleCN: 这封信以礼貌的称呼开头。
senses.why: The words one directs at a person are that person's address in speech.
senses.whyCN: 对人说出的称谓，就是称呼方式。

senses.title: To deal with a problem
senses.definition: to take action about a problem
senses.definitionCN: 针对某个问题采取行动
senses.example: The school must address the noise problem.
senses.exampleCN: 学校必须处理噪音问题。
senses.why: Pointing one's attention at a problem is the modern sense of dealing with it.
senses.whyCN: 把注意力指向问题，就是处理问题。

senses.title: To speak to a group
senses.definition: to make a speech to a group of people
senses.definitionCN: 对一群人发表讲话
senses.example: The mayor addressed the crowd.
senses.exampleCN: 市长对人群讲了话。
senses.why: Pointing one's voice at a crowd is the verb sense of speaking to them.
senses.whyCN: 把声音直指人群，就是对人群讲话。

intro.en: The recorded history of address is set out below; the deeper origin is marked where it is uncertain.
intro.cn: 下面是 address 有记录的历史；更早的来源存疑处已作标注。

items.en: The prefix ad- meant to or toward a point.
items.cn: 前缀 ad- 意为向或朝向某一点。

items.en: Directus meant straight or set in a line.
items.cn: directus 意为笔直的或排成一条线。

items.en: Adresser meant to set straight or to direct toward.
items.cn: adresser 意为摆正或指向。

items.en: English used address for directing words or letters to a person.
items.cn: 英语十四世纪用 address 指把话或信指向某人。

items.en: Today it also names home details and web locations.
items.cn: 今天它也指住址与网络地址。

note.en: The first group collects forms that look or sound alike; the second group collects words with a nearby meaning.
note.cn: 第一组收形近或音近的词，第二组收意义相近的词。

entries.definition: More than one place or speech.
entries.definitionCN: 指多个地址或演说。

entries.definition: The past form of the verb.
entries.definitionCN: 动词的过去式。

entries.definition: The person a letter is sent to.
entries.definitionCN: 指收件人。

entries.definition: It names a talk given to a group.
entries.definitionCN: 指对人群发表的讲话。

entries.definition: A plain word for the place where someone lives.
entries.definitionCN: 指某人居住之处的朴素说法。

entries.definition: It stresses dealing with a problem.
entries.definitionCN: 强调处理问题。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the recorded form, the real family and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用有记录的词形、真实的词族和这个词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: ad- means to and dresser means to direct: to address is to point something toward a place or a person.
normal.cn: ad- 表示向，dresser 表示指向：address 就是把事物朝向某地或某人。

normal.en: The same family also gives addressee and addressing.
normal.cn: 同一词族还给出 addressee 与 addressing。

normal.en: It often appears in the phrase home address.
normal.cn: 它常出现在「家庭住址」这个搭配里。

normal.en: Spell it as it sounds: keep every letter of address in order.
normal.cn: 按读音拼写：把 address 的每个字母按顺序保留。

normal.en: Use it when you mean: the place where someone lives, or a speech, or to deal with a problem.
normal.cn: 当你想表达「地址」时用它。

abstract.en: Picture an envelope with a clear line of writing for the address.
abstract.cn: 想象信封上写着一行清楚的地址。

abstract.en: The same picture can be literal in one sentence and figurative in another.
abstract.cn: 同一幅画面在一句里可以是字面意思，在另一句里可以是比喻。

abstract.en: Say the word aloud first, then let the picture bring the meaning back.
abstract.cn: 先把这个词读出声，再让画面把意思带回来。

examples.cn: 校长对全校发表了讲话。

branches.cn: 义项 02 覆盖更宽泛的日常用法：正式演说。

branches.en: Sense 03 covers a further use: A way of speaking to someone.
branches.cn: 义项 03 覆盖更靠后的一种用法：称呼方式。

definition_zh: 运动员；播放器；演奏者；参与者
definition_en: someone who takes part in a game or sport; also a device that plays recorded sound, a musician, or an active participant in a situation
core_image: 一个人站在场地中央，脚下有球，身后是等着看他下一步动作的观众
scene: 球场的看台渐渐坐满，替补席上有人不停活动脚踝。 The coach waved the young player onto the field in the final minutes.
sceneCN: 这里是「运动员、球员」（第 1 个义项）；句意为教练在最后几分钟挥手让这名年轻球员上场。图中可辨识物件：替补席、边线、球鞋。

pos.zh: 运动员；播放器；演奏者；参与者

derivatives.zh: player 的基础动词，义为「玩；比赛；播放」
由 play 加形容词后缀 -ful 构成，义为「爱玩的；戏谑的」
由 play 与 off 复合而成，义为「附加赛；季后赛」

senses.title: Someone who plays a sport or game
senses.definition: a person who takes part in a sport or a game, especially as a profession
senses.definitionCN: 参加体育运动或比赛的人，尤指以此为职业者
senses.example: Their best player was injured in the first half.
senses.exampleCN: 他们最好的球员在上半场受伤了。
senses.why: The suffix -er simply marks the person who does the verb, so a player is first of all one who plays, whether on a field or at a table.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -er 只标示做这个动作的人，所以 player 首先是「玩的人」，无论在球场上还是在牌桌旁。

senses.title: A device that reproduces sound or video
senses.definition: a machine or program that plays recorded music, films or files
senses.definitionCN: 播放录音、影片或文件的机器或程序
senses.example: He put the disc into the player and turned up the volume.
senses.exampleCN: 他把光盘放进播放器，调高了音量。
senses.why: When machines took over the act of playing music, the same person-suffix was attached to the device, as if the machine now did the playing.
senses.whyCN: 当机器接手「播放音乐」这个动作时，同一个表人的后缀被安到了机器上，仿佛现在由机器来扮演这个角色。

senses.title: A musician
senses.definition: a person who plays a musical instrument
senses.definitionCN: 演奏乐器的人
senses.example: She is a fine player of the cello.
senses.exampleCN: 她是一位出色的大提琴演奏者。
senses.why: Long before recordings, the one who played was a person with an instrument in hand, and this sense keeps the word close to the body and the fingers.
senses.whyCN: 在有录音之前，演奏的人就是手持乐器的人，这个义项让词始终贴近身体与手指。

senses.title: An active participant in a situation
senses.definition: a person or group that takes an active part in an activity, market or negotiation
senses.definitionCN: 积极介入某项活动、市场或谈判的人或团体
senses.example: The union is now a major player in the talks.
senses.exampleCN: 工会如今是谈判中的重要一方。
senses.why: From a game, the word widens to any contest of interests: whoever can make a move and change the outcome deserves to be called a player.
senses.whyCN: 从游戏出发，这个词扩展到任何利益博弈：谁能出手并改变结局，谁就配得上 player 这个称呼。

intro.en: Player is the plain English agent noun of play; the verb itself is old and its deeper origin is usually described as uncertain.
intro.cn: player 是 play 的英语施事名词，构词十分直接；动词 play 本身很古老，更早的来源一般被认为不确定。

items.en: The verb plegian meant to exercise, frolic or take part in a game.
items.cn: 动词 plegian 意为活动身体、嬉戏或参加游戏。

items.en: The related noun plega named a game, sport or quick movement.
items.cn: 相关名词 plega 指游戏、运动或轻快的动作。

items.en: Middle English play kept the sense of sport and amusement and began to cover music and performance.
items.cn: 中古英语 play 保留运动与娱乐义，并开始涵盖音乐与表演。

items.en: The native suffix -er, meaning one who does, made player out of play in the Middle English period.
items.cn: 本土后缀 -er 表示「做某事的人」，在中古英语时期把 play 变成了 player。

items.en: Modern English extends player to machines that reproduce sound and to anyone with a stake in a contest.
items.cn: 现代英语把 player 扩展到播放声音的机器，以及任何在一场较量中有份的人。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the play family and one word that only sounds close; the near-meaning group gathers people who perform, compete or take part.
note.cn: 形近组收 play 词族，以及一个只是读音相近的词；近义组收表演、竞争或参与的人。

entries.definition: To take part in a game, or to make music.
entries.definitionCN: 参加游戏；演奏。

entries.definition: Eager to play and joke rather than be serious.
entries.definitionCN: 爱玩爱闹的；戏谑的。

entries.definition: A list of songs chosen to be played in order.
entries.definitionCN: 按顺序播放的歌曲清单。

entries.definition: Words spoken to a god; sounds like player but comes from Latin precari.
entries.definitionCN: 向上帝或神说的话；读音近 player，但源自拉丁语 precari，词源不同。

entries.definition: A person trained in sports and physical games.
entries.definitionCN: 受过训练、擅长运动的人。

entries.definition: A person who sings, acts or plays for an audience.
entries.definitionCN: 为观众唱歌、表演或演奏的人。

entries.definition: A person competing for a prize.
entries.definitionCN: 争夺奖项的参赛者。

entries.definition: A person who takes part in an activity.
entries.definitionCN: 参加某项活动的人。

normalIntro.en: The word is play plus the person suffix, and every sense still asks the same question: who or what is doing the playing here?
normalIntro.cn: 这个词就是 play 加表人的后缀，每个义项都仍在问同一个问题：此刻是谁、是什么在「玩」？

normal.en: Player is play plus -er, the suffix for the one who does the action.
normal.cn: player 就是 play 加 -er，即「做这个动作的人」。

normal.en: A record player is a machine doing what a person used to do: playing the music.
normal.cn: 电唱机是一台机器在做过去由人做的事：播放音乐。

normal.en: A team player is not on the field but in the office: the image of a game is borrowed for cooperation.
normal.cn: team player 不在球场上而在办公室里：借用了比赛的画面来形容合作。

normal.en: Playful adds -ful, full of play, which shows how the family grows by short native suffixes.
normal.cn: playful 加 -ful，意为「充满玩的」，可见这个词族靠简短的本土后缀生长。

normal.en: Prayer is close in sound only; it comes from a Latin verb for begging and is not a relative.
normal.cn: prayer 只是读音相近，出自拉丁语中表示乞求的动词，并非同族词。

abstract.en: A word made by adding a person to an action reminds us that English often names a role before it names a thing.
abstract.cn: 给动作加上一个人，就造出一个词，这提醒人：英语常常先命名角色，再命名事物。

abstract.en: Calling a negotiator a player quietly turns a meeting into a game with moves and stakes.
abstract.cn: 把谈判者称作 player，悄悄把一场会议变成有招法、有输赢的游戏。

abstract.en: If a machine can be a player, then the word is less about being human than about taking the active part.
abstract.cn: 如果机器也能是 player，那么这个词的关键就不在于是不是人，而在于是否承担那个主动的角色。

examples.en: He is the youngest player on the national team.
examples.cn: 他是国家队里最年轻的球员。

examples.en: The old record player still works perfectly.
examples.cn: 那台旧电唱机仍然运转良好。

examples.en: She has become a key player in the peace talks.
examples.cn: 她已成为和平谈判中的关键人物。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「扑蕾尔」——场上那个人一扑一接，把球玩得团团转。

root: 英语本土词：play（古英语 plegian，活动、嬉戏）+ 表施事的后缀 -er；play 更早的来源一般认为不确定，尚无可靠的拉丁同族词。

sensesIntro.en: The core is one who plays; the senses then name the athlete, the machine that plays sound, the musician, and anyone with a move to make.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「玩的人」；义项由此指向运动员、播放声音的机器、乐手，以及任何有一步棋可走的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a figure standing in the middle of a field, ball at the feet, watched by people waiting for the next move.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人站在场地中央，脚下有球，身后是等他下一步动作的人。

branches.en: a substitute pulling off a training top
branches.cn: 替补球员脱下训练背心

branches.en: a small machine spinning a disc in a quiet room
branches.cn: 安静的房间里一台小机器转动唱片

branches.en: fingers finding the notes without looking
branches.cn: 手指不看谱就找到音位

branches.en: a name that can change the outcome of a deal
branches.cn: 一个能改变交易结局的名字

branches.en: the same word for a game and for a struggle of interests
branches.cn: 同一个词既用于比赛也用于利益较量

intro.cn: 这里全靠一个英语本土动词和一个本土后缀，不涉及拉丁前缀或词根。

latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

definition_zh: 纸；报纸；论文；试卷；文件；纸做的
definition_en: the thin material used for writing and printing, a newspaper, a written study or examination, official documents, and made of paper
core_image: 台灯下一叠白纸，边角被翻得起了毛
scene: 书桌的台灯下，一叠稿纸被翻得起了毛边，最上面那张只写了一个标题。 He pushed the paper aside and started again on a clean sheet.
sceneCN: 这里 paper 是「纸」（第 1 个义项：用来书写印刷的薄材料）；句意为他把那张纸推到一边，重新拿一张干净的纸从头写起。图中可辨识物件：台灯、起毛的稿纸、只写了标题的一页。

pos.zh: 纸做的；纸上的；名义上的
