paper 与 work 复合而成，指文书工作
news 与 paper 复合而成，指报纸
paper 与 back 复合而成，指纸面平装书

senses.title: The material used for writing
senses.definition: the thin material made from wood pulp or other fibres, used for writing, printing and wrapping
senses.definitionCN: 用木浆或其他纤维制成的薄材料，用于书写、印刷和包装
senses.example: He pushed the paper aside and started again on a clean sheet.
senses.exampleCN: 他把那张纸推到一边，重新拿一张干净的纸从头写起。
senses.why: The word began as papyrus, the Egyptian reed pressed into sheets, so the material itself is the oldest and most literal sense.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初是 papyrus，即埃及的那种芦苇，压成薄片用来书写，所以「材料」本身就是最古老、最字面的义项。

senses.title: A newspaper
senses.definition: a set of printed sheets published daily or weekly with news and comment
senses.definitionCN: 每日或每周出版、刊载新闻与评论的一套印刷纸张
senses.example: She reads the paper on the train every morning.
senses.exampleCN: 她每天早上在火车上看报纸。
senses.why: A newspaper is literally paper that carries news, so English kept the material's name for the daily object and dropped the first half of the compound.
senses.whyCN: 报纸字面上就是「载着新闻的纸」，英语把这个日刊直接叫作纸，省掉了复合词的前一半。

senses.title: A written study or an exam
senses.definition: a piece of academic writing on one topic, or the set of questions used in an examination
senses.definitionCN: 就一个题目写成的学术文章，或考试所用的一整套题目
senses.example: He published a paper on coastal erosion last year.
senses.exampleCN: 他去年发表了一篇关于海岸侵蚀的论文。
senses.why: A paper is a piece of writing that exists on paper; scholars hand in such sheets and examiners set them, so the same word covers both.
senses.whyCN: 论文就是写在纸上的一份文字；学者交上这样的纸页，出题人发出的也是这样的纸页，同一个词就同时覆盖了两边。

senses.title: Official documents
senses.definition: papers, the documents that prove who you are or what you are allowed to do
senses.definitionCN: 复数形式 papers，指证明身份或获准做某事的文件
senses.example: The guard asked to see her papers at the border.
senses.exampleCN: 边检人员要求看她的证件。
senses.why: Identity and permission are proved by printed sheets, so the plural papers came to mean the documents a person must carry.
senses.whyCN: 身份与许可都靠印好的纸页来证明，于是复数 papers 就指一个人必须随身携带的那些文件。

senses.title: Made of paper; existing only on paper
senses.titleCN: 纸做的；只停留在纸面上的
senses.definition: made of paper, or true only in written records and not in real life
senses.definitionCN: 用纸做的；或只在书面记录中成立、在现实中并不成立
senses.example: They handed out paper cups at the entrance.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在入口处发放纸杯。
senses.why: When something exists only as figures on a sheet, it is paper in the adjective's sense: it looks solid but has no body behind it.
senses.whyCN: 当某样东西只以纸上的数字存在时，它就是这个形容词意义上的 paper：看上去实在，背后却没有实体。

intro.en: Paper is named after papyrus, the reed of the Nile; Greek papuros passed into Latin as papyrus and into English through Old French papier.
intro.cn: paper 得名于尼罗河的纸莎草；希腊语 papuros 进入拉丁语作 papyrus，又经古法语 papier 进入英语。

items.en: Papuros was the Egyptian reed whose pith was pressed into writing sheets, and Greek used the same word for the sheets.
items.cn: papuros 是埃及的芦苇，其茎髓被压成书写用的薄片，希腊语也用同一个词指这些薄片。

items.en: Latin took papyrus from Greek for both the plant and the writing material sold across the empire.
items.cn: 拉丁语从希腊语借来 papyrus，同时指这种植物和在帝国各地出售的书写材料。

items.en: Old French papier named the material, and Norman scribes brought the word to England.
items.cn: 古法语 papier 指这种材料，诺曼抄写员把这个词带到了英格兰。

items.en: Middle English paper covered the sheets and, as printing spread, the newspaper and the written study.
items.cn: 中古英语的 paper 指纸页，随着印刷术传播，也指报纸与写成的研究。

items.en: Modern English keeps papers for documents and adds paper as an adjective for anything that exists only on a page.
items.cn: 现代英语用 papers 指文件，并把 paper 用作形容词，指只存在于纸面上的东西。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the reed, the material and the things made from it; the near-meaning group gathers other words for sheets and written records.
note.cn: 形近组沿芦苇、材料以及用它做成的东西展开；近义组收其他表示纸页与书面记录的词。

entries.definition: The ancient writing material made from pressed reed, which gave paper its name.
entries.definitionCN: 用压制芦苇制成的古代书写材料，正是 paper 得名的来源。

entries.definition: Thin, dry and light, like paper.
entries.definitionCN: 薄、干、轻，像纸一样。

entries.definition: A printed publication of news, literally news on paper.
entries.definitionCN: 刊载新闻的印刷出版物，字面就是印在纸上的新闻。

entries.definition: A book with a thin flexible cover rather than a hard one.
entries.definitionCN: 用薄软封面而非硬壳装订的书。

entries.definition: A single flat piece of paper, cloth or other thin material.
entries.definitionCN: 纸、布等薄材料的单张平面。

entries.definition: An official record of information, now often kept as a computer file.
entries.definitionCN: 信息的正式记录，如今常以电子文件形式保存。

entries.definition: A periodical publishing scholarly articles in a field.
entries.definitionCN: 在某一领域刊载学术文章的期刊。

normalIntro.en: The word began as the name of a reed, survived as the name of the sheet, and then lent itself to everything printed on that sheet.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词最初是一种芦苇的名字，后来成为纸页的名字，再借给写在纸页上的一切。

normal.en: Papyrus was a Nile reed, and paper keeps its name even after the reed was replaced by rags and wood pulp.
normal.cn: papyrus 是一种尼罗河芦苇，即使原料早已换成破布与木浆，paper 仍留着它的名字。

normal.en: A newspaper is literally paper that carries news, which is why the material's name survived in the daily.
normal.cn: 报纸字面上就是载着新闻的纸，所以「材料」的名字留在了这份日刊里。

normal.en: Papers in the plural means documents, the sheets you must show at a border.
normal.cn: 复数 papers 指文件，也就是在边境必须拿出来给人看的那几张纸。

normal.en: A paper can be a study you publish, because scholarship once travelled as printed sheets.
normal.cn: paper 也可以指你发表的论文，因为学问曾经就靠印好的纸页传播。

normal.en: On paper marks a plan that has not yet met the world.
normal.cn: on paper 标出一个还没和现实碰面的计划。

abstract.en: Paper is a surface that holds a thought longer than a voice can.
abstract.cn: 纸是一种表面，能让一个想法留存得比声音更久。

abstract.en: A sheet is cheap, which is why it can carry both a shopping list and a treaty.
abstract.cn: 一张纸很便宜，所以它既能承载购物清单，也能承载条约。

abstract.en: To say something is only on paper is to doubt whether the page can change anything.
abstract.cn: 说某件事只停留在纸面上，就是在怀疑这页纸能否改变任何东西。

examples.en: He pushed the paper aside and started again on a clean sheet.
examples.cn: 他把那张纸推到一边，重新拿一张干净的纸从头写起。

examples.en: He published a paper on coastal erosion last year.
examples.cn: 他去年发表了一篇关于海岸侵蚀的论文。

examples.en: The deal looked good on paper but failed in practice.
examples.cn: 这笔交易在纸面上看着不错，实际操作却失败了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「佩珀」——像胡椒一样又薄又轻的一张，一吹就飘走；记住 paper 是纸。

root: 希腊语 papuros（纸莎草）— 拉丁语 papyrus — 古法语 papier — 英语 paper。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the sheet you can write on; the senses then move to the daily printed sheet, the study written on it, the documents you carry, and finally the adjective for what exists only there.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是可以书写的纸页；义项随后转到每日印出的那张纸、写在上面的研究、随身携带的文件，最后是「只存在于纸上」的形容词用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stack of white sheets under a lamp, edges soft from being turned.
core.cn: 核心意象：台灯下一叠白纸，边角因反复翻动而发毛。

branches.en: a blank sheet waiting under a lamp
branches.cn: 台灯下等着的空白纸

branches.en: a folded daily on a train seat
branches.cn: 火车座位上折起的日报

branches.en: a printed study with a long reference list
branches.cn: 印着长串参考文献的研究论文

branches.en: passports checked at a border desk
branches.cn: 边检台上被查验的护照

branches.en: a cup made of paper and a promise made of ink
branches.cn: 纸做的杯子与墨水写成的承诺

intro.en: The word travels from a Greek reed name through Latin and French, and English then builds compounds that name the things printed on the sheet.
intro.cn: 这个词从希腊语的芦苇名出发，经拉丁语和法语转手，英语再用它造出指纸上各类印刷物的复合词。

latinIntro.en: Latin papyrus is itself a borrowing from Greek papuros, and it names both the reed and the writing material made from it.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 papyrus 本身借自希腊语 papuros，兼指这种芦苇和用它制成的书写材料。

definition_zh: 沙漠；荒漠；荒凉之地
definition_en: a large dry area of land with few plants because there is little rain
core_image: 一眼望不到边的金色沙丘
scene: 地理课上我们看了骆驼穿越沙丘的照片。 A camel can walk for days across the hot desert with little water.
sceneCN: 这里 desert 是「沙漠」（第 1 个义项：少雨干旱之地）；句意是骆驼能在炎热的沙漠里几乎没有水地走上好几天。

derivatives.zh: 由 desert 加形容词后缀 -ed 构成，义为「无人的；被遗弃的」
由 desert 加 -fication 构成，义为「沙漠化」
拼写相近的另一个词，义为「甜点」

senses.title: A large dry land
senses.definition: a large area of land with very little rain and few plants
senses.definitionCN: 降雨极少、植物稀少的大片土地
senses.example: The desert is cold at night even in summer.
senses.exampleCN: 即使在夏天，沙漠的夜晚也很冷。
senses.why: Land abandoned by rain is left dry and empty, so it was called a deserted place.
senses.whyCN: 被雨水「抛弃」的土地变得干燥空旷，人们便称它为被遗弃之地，即沙漠。

senses.title: An empty, lonely place
senses.definition: any place that seems empty and without life
senses.definitionCN: 任何显得空旷而没有生气的地方
senses.example: At noon the playground was a desert of silence.
senses.exampleCN: 中午的操场是一片寂静的空旷。
senses.why: Emptiness borrows the desert picture wherever life is missing.
senses.whyCN: 凡是缺少生气的地方都借来沙漠的画面，于是有了荒凉空旷的比喻义。

intro.en: Desert comes from Latin words for leaving and abandoning.
intro.cn: desert 来自拉丁语中表示「离开、抛弃」的词。

items.en: De- means away, and serere means to join or plant; desertus meant abandoned.
items.cn: 拉丁语 de- 表示离开，serere 意为结合、种植；desertus 意为被抛弃的。

items.en: Desertum named land forsaken by people or by rain.
items.cn: desertum 指被人或雨水抛弃的土地。

items.en: Old French desert meant emptiness and abandonment.
items.cn: 古法语 desert 意为空旷、遗弃。

items.en: English took the word in the thirteenth century for wild empty land.
items.cn: 英语在十三世纪吸收该词，指荒芜空旷之地。

items.en: It narrowed to the hot sandy kind of empty land we call desert today.
items.cn: 现代英语中它缩小为今天所说的炎热多沙的沙漠。

note.en: These words share the leaving root or describe dry empty land.
note.cn: 这些词与「离开」词根同源，或同样描述干旱空旷的土地。

entries.definition: sweet food after a meal, different root
entries.definitionCN: 甜点（拼写相近，词源不同）

entries.definition: with no people
entries.definitionCN: 无人的；被遗弃的

entries.definition: the act of leaving
entries.definitionCN: 遗弃；开小差

entries.definition: to earn something, different root
entries.definitionCN: 应得（拼写相近，词源无关）

entries.definition: a small spoon, from dessert
entries.definitionCN: 点心匙

entries.definition: wild empty land
entries.definitionCN: 荒野

entries.definition: barren land
entries.definitionCN: 荒地

entries.definition: a green wet spot in a desert
entries.definitionCN: 绿洲（相对概念）

entries.definition: producing little or nothing
entries.definitionCN: 贫瘠的

entries.definition: left and not used
entries.definitionCN: 被遗弃的

normalIntro.en: Use the sand image and the one-s rule to remember desert.
normalIntro.cn: 用「沙丘」的画面和单 s 规则记住 desert。

normal.en: desert with one s is dry sand.
normal.cn: 一个 s 的 desert 是干燥的沙漠。

normal.en: dessert with two s is sweet food you want seconds of.
normal.cn: 两个 s 的 dessert 是想再来一份的甜点。

normal.en: the Sahara is the biggest hot desert.
normal.cn: 撒哈拉是最大的炎热沙漠。

normal.en: camels are ships of the desert.
normal.cn: 骆驼被称为沙漠之舟。

normal.en: deserted means empty of people.
normal.cn: deserted 表示无人的。

abstract.en: Picture golden dunes rolling to the horizon.
abstract.cn: 想象金色沙丘绵延到地平线。

abstract.en: Feel the hot day turn into a cold night.
abstract.cn: 体会沙漠白天炎热、夜里转凉的变化。

abstract.en: Hear the wind brushing across empty sand.
abstract.cn: 听风掠过空旷沙面的声音。

examples.en: Some deserts get less rain in a year than we get in one afternoon.
examples.cn: 有些沙漠一年的降水还不如我们一个下午的雨多。

examples.en: The story is about a boy who crossed a desert to find water for his village.
examples.cn: 这个故事讲一个男孩穿越沙漠为村子找水。

examples.en: After the fair left, the field looked like a desert of torn paper.
examples.cn: 集市散场后，场地像一片纸屑的荒漠。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「低泽特」——地势低洼没水泽，就成了「沙漠」

root: 来自拉丁语 desertum（被抛弃之地），由 de-（离开）加 serere（结合、种植）派生；「雨水离开的土地」即沙漠。

sensesIntro.en: Desert begins as abandoned land and stretches to any empty place.
sensesIntro.cn: desert 先指被遗弃的土地，再延伸到一切空旷之地。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: land left behind by rain
core.cn: 核心意象：被雨水遗弃的土地

branches.en: Sand, sun and camels
branches.cn: 沙、太阳与骆驼

branches.en: Any silent empty space
branches.cn: 寂静空旷之处

branches.en: Cold nights after hot days
branches.cn: 炎热白昼后的寒夜

branches.en: Where life is scarce
branches.cn: 生命稀少之地

branches.en: Loneliness you can see
branches.cn: 看得见的孤独

intro.en: Desert is built on the Latin root for leaving.
intro.cn: desert 建立在拉丁语「离开」词根上。

latinIntro.en: The Latin root ser or sert means to join, to plant.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词根 ser/sert 意为结合、种植。

camp in the wilderness（在荒野露营）

definition_zh: 圣诞节；圣诞时期
definition_en: a Christian festival on December 25 celebrating the birth of Jesus Christ
core_image: 雪花里的圣诞树，树下堆着礼物
scene: 十二月末，教室门口挂起了彩灯和花环。 We will sing songs at the Christmas party.
sceneCN: 这里 Christmas 是「圣诞节」（第 1 个义项：十二月二十五日纪念耶稣诞生的节日）；句意是我们将在圣诞聚会上唱歌。

derivatives.zh: 由 Christmas 加 time 构成，义为「圣诞时节」
由 Christmas 加后缀 -y 构成，义为「有圣诞气氛的」
古英语同源旧词，义为「圣诞节（古称）」

senses.title: The festival on December 25
senses.definition: the yearly Christian holiday celebrating the birth of Jesus
senses.definitionCN: 每年纪念耶稣诞生的基督教节日
senses.example: Christmas falls on December 25 this year.
senses.exampleCN: 今年圣诞节是十二月二十五日。
senses.why: The basic sense names the fixed festival day directly.
senses.whyCN: 基本义项直接命名了这个固定的节日。

senses.title: The holiday season around it
senses.definition: the days and weeks around December 25 when people celebrate
senses.definitionCN: 十二月二十五日前后人们庆祝活动的那些日子
senses.example: The whole family gathers at Christmas.
senses.exampleCN: 圣诞节期间全家人团聚。
senses.why: A single day grows into a season of parties and rest.
senses.whyCN: 一天的生长出围绕它的一整段聚会与休息的时节。

senses.title: The cultural celebration of giving
senses.titleCN: 圣诞庆祝活动（礼物、聚会）
senses.definition: the customs of gifts, meals and celebrations connected with the festival
senses.definitionCN: 与节日相关的送礼、聚餐、庆祝等习俗
senses.example: Children hung stockings for Christmas.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们为过节挂起了长袜。
senses.why: Customs become so central that the festival's name covers them.
senses.whyCN: 习俗太过核心，节日之名便把这一切都涵盖进去。

intro.en: Christmas is a very transparent name: it is the mass of Christ.
intro.cn: Christmas 的名字非常直白：它就是「基督的弥撒」。

items.en: Old English Cristes mæsse meant the mass of Christ.
items.cn: 古英语 Cristes mæsse 义为「基督的弥撒」。

items.en: The phrase fused into one word, written Christemasse in Middle English.
items.cn: 这个短语融合成一词，中古英语写作 Christemasse。

items.en: Behind the English lies Latin Christus, from Greek Christos, the anointed one.
items.cn: 其背后是拉丁语 Christus，源自希腊语 Christos，义为「受膏者」。

items.en: The word mass comes from Latin missa, the church service of the Eucharist.
items.cn: mass 一词来自拉丁语 missa，指圣餐礼拜仪式。

items.en: Modern English keeps the fused form Christmas since the sixteenth century.
items.cn: 十六世纪以来现代英语保留融合形式 Christmas。

note.en: The first group gathers look-alike spellings; the second gathers festival words.
note.cn: 第一组收形近词，第二组收节日类词。

entries.definition: Having a Christmas feeling.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「有圣诞气氛的」，是 Christmas 加 -y。

entries.definition: To give a baby a name in church.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「为婴儿洗礼命名」，词首相近但词源不同。

entries.definition: A person believing in Christ.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「基督徒」，与 Christmas 同含 Christ 词根。

entries.definition: The festival on January 1.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「新年」，紧随圣诞之后的节日。

entries.definition: The spring Christian festival.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「复活节」，另一基督教大节。

entries.definition: An old word for Christmas.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，圣诞节的古称，源自古英语。

normalIntro.en: Remember Christmas as Christ plus mass.
normalIntro.cn: 把 Christmas 拆成 Christ 加 mass 来记。

normal.en: Christ + mas(s): the mass of Christ.
normal.cn: Christ 加 mas(s)，即「基督的弥撒」。

normal.en: The t is often silent in speech: KRIS-mus.
normal.cn: 口语中 t 常不发音，读 KRIS-mus。

normal.en: Christmas Eve is the night before the festival.
normal.cn: Christmas Eve 指圣诞前夜，即平安夜。

normal.en: Merry Christmas is the standard greeting.
normal.cn: Merry Christmas 是标准祝福语。

normal.en: Xmas is a short written form, best for notes.
normal.cn: Xmas 是简写形式，适合便条使用。

abstract.en: See a fir tree glowing with small coloured lights.
abstract.cn: 想象一棵挂满彩色小灯的枞树发着光。

abstract.en: Hear bells and carols over snowy streets.
abstract.cn: 仿佛听见雪街上飘来的钟声与颂歌。

abstract.en: Feel the paper rip as presents open at dawn.
abstract.cn: 感受清晨拆礼物时纸声刺啦的兴奋。

examples.en: We decorate the Christmas tree together every year.
examples.cn: 我们每年一起装饰圣诞树。

examples.en: My aunt sent me a Christmas card from Beijing.
examples.cn: 姑姑从北京给我寄来一张圣诞贺卡。

examples.en: Christmas is a time for family dinners.
examples.cn: 圣诞节是一家人聚餐的时光。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「克里斯莫斯」——克里斯在莫名的雪夜里拆礼物，过圣诞。

root: 古英语 Cristes mæsse（基督的弥撒）→ 中古英语 Christemasse → 现代英语 Christmas；Christ 源自希腊语 Christos（受膏者），mass 源自拉丁语 missa（弥撒）。

sensesIntro.en: Christmas names the day itself, the season around it and its customs of giving.

senses.exampleCN: 她在学校的话剧中表演。

senses.whyCN: 把「做」放在观众面前，就变成舞台上的表演。

senses.definitionCN: 对某物产生作用

senses.title: To play a role

senses.why: Performing a named character is the actor's narrower form of acting.
senses.whyCN: 表演具体到某个有名有姓的角色，就是扮演。

senses.title: A law

senses.whyCN: 议会正式「做出」的决定成为法律，就是法案。

sceneCN: 这里是「力量、气力」（第 4 个义项：身体的力气）；句意为他用尽全力抵住那扇摇动的门。图中可辨识物件：抵门的肩膀、晃动的门板、仓库门。

senses.title: Possibility that something is true or may happen
senses.definition: used to say that something is possible, though the speaker is not certain it is true or will happen
senses.definitionCN: 表示某事有可能发生或成立，但说话人并不确定
senses.example: It might rain before we reach the station.
senses.exampleCN: 我们到车站之前可能会下雨。
senses.why: Might is the past form of may, and English uses a past form to make a statement sound less sure, so the word moves from permission to a guarded guess.
senses.whyCN: might 是 may 的过去式，而英语常用过去形式让陈述听起来不那么确定，于是这个词从「许可」转向「留有余地的猜测」。

senses.title: A polite request or a hesitant suggestion
senses.definition: used to ask for something or suggest an action in a careful, polite way
senses.definitionCN: 用于小心、客气地提出请求或建议
senses.example: Might I borrow your umbrella for an hour?
senses.exampleCN: 我可以借你的伞用一个小时吗？
senses.why: The same past form softens the demand; by placing the request in a distant tense, the speaker leaves the listener free to refuse.
senses.whyCN: 同一个过去式把要求放软：把请求放进一个较远的时态里，就等于给听者留下拒绝的余地。

senses.title: A past possibility that was not taken
senses.definition: used with have to say that something was possible or should have happened but did not
senses.definitionCN: 与 have 连用，表示某事本来可能发生或本该发生，却没有发生
senses.example: You might have told me the meeting had moved.
senses.exampleCN: 你本可以告诉我会议改了时间。
senses.why: Once might marks unreal possibility, adding have fixes that unreal possibility in the past, and the speaker can point at a road that was open and was not walked.
senses.whyCN: 既然 might 标记「非现实的」可能性，再接上 have 就把这种可能固定在过去，说话人便能指向一条曾经敞开、却没被走的路。

senses.title: Great physical power or strength
senses.definition: great physical strength or force, especially when gathered for a single effort
senses.definitionCN: 巨大的体力或力量，尤指为一次发力而聚集起来
senses.example: He pushed with all his might against the swinging door.
senses.exampleCN: 他用尽全力抵住那扇摇动的门。
senses.why: Before it was a modal verb, might was a noun meaning power, and the noun still keeps the older body sense that the modal has left behind.
senses.whyCN: 在成为情态动词之前，might 本是一个意为「力量」的名词；这个名词至今保留着情态动词早已丢下的、属于身体的那层意思。

intro.en: Might began as an Old English noun for power and as a past form of may, and the two meanings have stayed side by side.
intro.cn: might 起初既是古英语中表示「力量」的名词，又是 may 的过去式，这两种身份一直并存。

items.en: A reconstructed root for being able is generally proposed behind the Germanic words for power, though its exact shape remains uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为，日耳曼语中表示「有能力」的词背后有一个重构词根，但其确切形态仍不确定。

items.en: The noun for power stood beside a verb meaning to be able, and the two supplied the family of may and might.
items.cn: 表示力量的名词与表示「有能力」的动词并列存在，二者共同供出了 may 与 might 的词族。

items.en: Old English meaht meant power, strength or ability, and miht was its variant spelling.
items.cn: 古英语 meaht 意为力量、力气、能力，miht 是它的变体拼写。

items.en: Middle English kept the noun might for power while also using it as the past form of may in conditional statements.
items.cn: 中古英语保留名词 might 表示力量，同时把它当作 may 的过去式，用在条件句里。

items.en: Modern English made the modal use dominant and left the noun in fixed phrases such as 「with all one's might」.
items.cn: 现代英语让情态动词用法占了主导，名词则退守到「with all one's might」这类固定短语里。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the family of may and might plus a compound built on mighty; the near-meaning group collects words for power and for possibility.
note.cn: 形近组收 may 与 might 的同族词，外加一个由 mighty 构成的复合词；近义组收表示力量与表示可能的词。

entries.definition: Very strong or powerful.
entries.definitionCN: 非常强壮或有力量的。

entries.definition: With great force, or very much.
entries.definitionCN: 以巨大的力量，或非常地。

entries.definition: Having complete power, formed from all and mighty.
entries.definitionCN: 拥有全然的力量，由 all 与 mighty 构成。

entries.definition: The ability to act or to control people and events.
entries.definitionCN: 行动或控制人与事件的能力。

entries.definition: The physical force that a body or a material can use or bear.

entries.definition: Energy applied to move something or to make a change happen.
entries.definitionCN: 为移动某物或促成改变而施加的能量。

entries.definition: Another past-form modal used for possibility and for polite requests.
entries.definitionCN: 另一个用过去形式表示可能与委婉请求的情态动词。

normalIntro.en: The word carries two lives, a noun for bodily power and a past form of may; the family keeps returning to what a person is able to do and what may therefore happen.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词身负两重身份：一个是表示身体力量的名词，一个是 may 的过去式；同族词反复回到人能做到什么，以及因此可能发生什么。

normal.en: Might is the past form of may, and English uses a past form to sound less certain.
normal.cn: might 是 may 的过去式，英语用过去形式来让语气显得不那么确定。

normal.en: The noun might meant power long before the modal sense appeared, and the two live on in the same spelling.
normal.cn: 名词 might 在情态用法出现之前就指力量，两种身份共用同一个拼写，一直活到今天。

normal.en: The phrase 「with all one's might」 is the noun in fixed form, where might still means bodily strength.
normal.cn: 「with all one's might」是名词用法的固定形式，这里的 might 仍指身体的力量。

normal.en: Mighty adds -y to might, turning power into an adjective, and mightily adds -ly in turn.
normal.cn: mighty 在 might 后加 -y，把力量变成形容词，mightily 再在其后加 -ly。

normal.en: 「Might have done」 points at a road that was open in the past and was not taken.
normal.cn: 「might have done」指向一条过去曾经敞开、却没有被走的路。

abstract.en: A single word for power and for possibility suggests that what is possible is what a person is able to bring about.
abstract.cn: 一个同时表示力量与可能的词说明：所谓可能，就是人有能力促成的范围。

abstract.en: The modal keeps a past form to sound humble, a reminder that grammar itself can lower a voice.
abstract.cn: 情态动词用过去形式来显得谦逊，这提醒人：语法本身也能把声音放低。

abstract.en: Might have says that history holds unused doors, and the word lets a speaker stand in front of one.
abstract.cn: might have 说明过去握着一些没被推开的门，这个词让说话人站到其中一扇门前。

intro.en: The word is carried by an Old English noun of power, the verb beside it, the past form of may, and two English endings that build the adjective and the adverb.

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for might: the word belongs to the Germanic branch, so the Latin side is left empty.
latinIntro.cn: might 没有可靠的拉丁同族词，它属于日耳曼语这一支，因此拉丁同源部分留空。

definition_zh: 西装；套装；适合；诉讼
definition_en: a set of matching clothes, or to be right for someone
core_image: 一套剪裁合体的西装挂在衣架上
scene: 这套西装很合他的身。 The suit fits him well.
sceneCN: 这里 suit 是「西装套装」（第 1 个义项）；句意：这套西装很合他的身。

senses.title: A set of matching clothes
senses.definition: a jacket with matching trousers or skirt
senses.definitionCN: 上衣与裤子或裙子成套的衣服
senses.example: The suit fits him well.
senses.exampleCN: 这套西装很合他的身。
senses.why: This is the most familiar noun sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是最常见的名词义项。

senses.title: To be right for someone
senses.definition: to be convenient or right for a person
senses.definitionCN: 对某人来说方便或合适
senses.example: Morning suits me better than evening.
senses.exampleCN: 早上比晚上更适合我。
senses.why: This verb sense is about personal fit.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词义项说的是对人的合适。

senses.title: To match in style
senses.definition: to look good together with something
senses.definitionCN: 在颜色或风格上协调
senses.example: The tie suits his shirt.
senses.exampleCN: 这条领带与他的衬衫很配。
senses.why: Here the word is about visual harmony.
senses.whyCN: 这里说的是视觉上的协调。

senses.title: A legal case
senses.definition: a case brought to a court of law
senses.definitionCN: 提交法院审理的案件
senses.example: She filed a suit against the company.
senses.exampleCN: 她对公司提起了诉讼。
senses.why: This is the fixed legal use of the word.
senses.whyCN: 这是该词在法律领域的固定用法。

items.cn: sequi 意为跟随。

items.en: Suite meant a following or a set.
items.cn: suite 意为随行的人或一套。

items.cn: suite 保留了序列的含义。

items.en: Sute named a matching set of clothes.

items.en: Suit came to mean a business suit and to fit.
